questions.q: Which Microsoft Office application is used primarily for word processing?
questions.e: Word is the Office application built for text-based documents such as letters and reports, distinct from Excel (spreadsheets), Access (databases) and PowerPoint (presentations).

questions.q: Which application is used for database management?
questions.e: Access is Microsoft's database management application, used for storing, querying and reporting on structured records.

questions.q: Which application handles slide presentations?
questions.e: PowerPoint is the Office application for building and delivering slide presentations.

questions.q: Which application manages email, calendar and contacts?
questions.e: Outlook is the Office application for email, calendar, contacts and task management.

questions.q: Which application is used for desktop publishing tasks like flyers and newsletters?
questions.e: Publisher is Microsoft's desktop publishing application, purpose-built for flyers, newsletters, brochures and posters.

questions.q: In a spreadsheet, what do we call the point where a row and a column meet?
questions.e: The intersection of a row and a column is called a cell, and it is identified by its column letter and row number, e.g. B4.

questions.q: Budgets, balance sheets, trial balance and payroll are examples of spreadsheet use in which field?
questions.e: Budgets, balance sheets, trial balance, cash flow, costing and payroll are all classic accounting uses of a spreadsheet.

questions.q: Computing standard deviation, variance, ANOVA and regression are examples of spreadsheet use in which field?
questions.e: Averages, standard deviation, variance, R², ANOVA, regression and frequency tables are scientific/statistical uses of a spreadsheet.

questions.q: A hospital plotting a pie chart or line graph of mortality and morbidity trends is using a spreadsheet for what purpose?
questions.e: Turning numbers into pie charts, histograms and line graphs to track trends like mortality and morbidity is a graphical-representation use of spreadsheets.

questions.q: Sizing a storm drain for different rainfall rates by changing one input and observing the effect on the result is an example of:
questions.e: Changing one input to instantly see its effect on an outcome, such as storm drain sizing or profit forecasting, is called 'what-if' analysis.

questions.q: Which of these was NOT one of the early spreadsheet packages that predated Excel?
questions.e: AS-EASY-AS, SUPERCALC, LOTUS 1-2-3, SYMPHONY, QUATROPRO and FRAMEWORK IV were all earlier spreadsheet packages; Word is a word processor, not a spreadsheet.

questions.q: What is the maximum number of characters you can type into a single Excel cell?
questions.e: A single Excel cell can hold up to 255 characters of text.

questions.q: Under Excel's default General number format, how is plain text aligned in a cell?
questions.e: Under the General format, text is left-aligned by default while numbers are right-aligned, giving a quick visual cue for the data type.

questions.q: Which entry forces the number 25,000 to be stored and treated as text rather than a value?
questions.e: Prefixing a number with an apostrophe, e.g. '25,000, forces Excel to store and left-align it as text instead of a calculable value.

questions.q: A column is too narrow to display a large number. What might Excel show instead?
o: A blank cell showing nothing at all
The number wraps automatically onto two lines
questions.e: When a number is too wide for its column, Excel displays #### signs or switches to scientific notation such as 2.17E+09.

questions.q: Excel stores dates as serial numbers counting from which date as day 1?
questions.e: Excel's date serial numbers begin counting from 1 January 1900, which is serial number 1.

questions.q: How does Excel store a time value internally?
o: As a whole number of minutes since midnight
As a decimal fraction of a 24-hour day
questions.e: Excel represents a time of day as the decimal fraction of a full 24-hour day that has elapsed, e.g. noon = 0.5.

questions.q: What decimal fraction represents 12:00 noon in Excel's time storage?
questions.e: Noon is exactly halfway through a 24-hour day, so it is stored as the decimal fraction 0.5.

questions.q: Which shortcut key applies the date format to the selected cell?
questions.e: Ctrl+# applies the date format to the selected cell.

questions.q: Which shortcut key applies the time format to the selected cell?
questions.e: Ctrl+@ applies the time format to the selected cell.

questions.q: Which shortcut key inserts today's date into the active cell?
questions.e: Ctrl+; inserts the current date into the active cell.

questions.q: Which shortcut key inserts the current time into the active cell?
questions.e: Ctrl+: inserts the current time into the active cell.

questions.q: Which of the following is a valid date entry format Excel recognises?
questions.e: Excel recognises formats such as m/d/yy, dd/mm/yy, d-mmm-yy and mmmm d yyyy as valid dates.

questions.q: Which of the following is a valid time entry format Excel recognises?
questions.e: Excel recognises time formats such as h:mm, h:mm:ss AM/PM and [h]:mm:ss.

questions.q: As you type text into a cell, Excel proposes the rest of a matching entry already used elsewhere in that column. What feature is this?
questions.e: This is AutoComplete: Excel checks earlier entries in the same column and suggests a completion as you type.

questions.q: How do you accept an AutoComplete suggestion Excel has proposed in a cell?
questions.e: Pressing Enter (or Tab) accepts the AutoComplete suggestion and places the full matched entry in the cell.

questions.q: How do you override an AutoComplete suggestion instead of accepting it?
questions.e: Continuing to type your own text overrides the suggested completion, replacing it with your keystrokes.

questions.q: Where do you go to turn AutoComplete off entirely?
questions.e: AutoComplete is disabled via File > Options > Advanced, by unchecking 'Enable AutoComplete for cell values'.

questions.q: A date-and-time serial value combines a whole number and a decimal. What does the decimal portion represent?
o: An offset applied to the year value
The day of the week it falls on
The month number of the date
The time of day as a fraction of 24 hours
questions.e: The whole-number part of a date/time serial value is the date, while the decimal part represents the time of day as a fraction of a 24-hour day.

questions.q: Which keyboard key(s) clear the contents of a selected cell without removing the cell itself?
questions.e: Del or Backspace clears a cell's contents while leaving the cell itself in place in the grid.

questions.q: Which Clear command option removes only the font, colour and number formatting of a cell while keeping its value?
questions.e: Clear Formats removes formatting such as font, colour, borders and number format, but leaves the cell's content untouched.

questions.q: Which command removes a cell entirely from the grid, requiring neighbouring cells to shift left or up?
questions.e: Delete removes the cell itself, so surrounding cells must shift to fill the resulting gap, unlike Clear which just empties the cell.

questions.q: In the Delete dialog box, which of these is NOT one of the available options?
questions.e: The Delete dialog offers Shift cells left, Shift cells up, Entire row and Entire column; 'Fill Formatting Only' is an Auto Fill Options choice, not a Delete option.

questions.q: What is the Fill Handle?
o: A menu command for inserting rows
A dialog box for renaming worksheets
The small solid square at the bottom-right corner of a selected cell
The button that saves a workbook
questions.e: The Fill Handle is the small solid square at the bottom-right corner of a selected cell or range, used for dragging to copy or extend data.

questions.q: Where in Excel do you enable or disable the Fill Handle and cell drag-and-drop feature?
questions.e: The Fill Handle and cell drag-and-drop feature is switched on or off in Excel's Options.

questions.q: After dragging the Fill Handle, which Auto Fill Option copies the source cell's colours and borders but not its value?
questions.e: Fill Formatting Only copies the source cell's formatting into the filled cells without copying its underlying value.

questions.q: Which Auto Fill Option copies the filled values while leaving each destination cell's own existing formatting untouched?
questions.e: Fill Without Formatting copies the value or series into the target cells while keeping each cell's own formatting unchanged.

questions.q: Which keyboard shortcut fills a selected range downward from the topmost cell?
questions.e: Ctrl+D fills the selected range downward, copying the topmost cell's content into the cells below it.

questions.q: Which keyboard shortcut fills a selected range to the right from the leftmost cell?
questions.e: Ctrl+R fills the selected range to the right, copying the leftmost cell's content across the row.

questions.q: A cell contains the formula =B2*C2. Dragging its Fill Handle down the column will:
o: Copy the formula to each row, adjusting the relative references automatically
Copy the exact same formula unchanged to every row
Convert the formula into a fixed value in every row
Delete the formula from the original cell
questions.e: Dragging a formula's Fill Handle down a column copies the formula to each row while automatically adjusting its relative cell references.

questions.q: What is the quickest way to auto-fill a formula all the way down to match an adjacent filled column, without manually dragging?
questions.e: Double-clicking the Fill Handle auto-fills the formula down to match the length of an adjacent filled column, without manual dragging.

questions.q: In the Insert dialog box, what happens if you choose 'Shift cells down'?
o: Existing cells in that range move up
New blank cells are inserted and existing cells move down
Only formatting is inserted, not values
questions.e: Choosing Shift cells down in the Insert dialog inserts new blank cells at the selection and pushes the existing cells downward.

questions.q: Which Clear command option removes any notes attached to a cell without touching its value or formatting?
questions.e: Clear Comments removes only attached notes/comments, leaving the cell's value and formatting untouched.

questions.q: Which of these correctly distinguishes Clear from Delete?
o: Clear empties a cell but keeps it in place; Delete removes the cell and shifts neighbours
Clear and Delete always do exactly the same thing
Delete only works on entire columns
Clear can only be used on formulas
questions.e: Clear removes what is inside a cell but leaves the cell itself in place, while Delete removes the cell itself, requiring neighbouring cells to shift.

questions.q: You type 0, 1, 2, 3 into four cells, select them, and drag the Fill Handle. What does Excel continue with?
questions.e: Excel recognises the counting pattern from the selected values and continues it: 4, 5, 6, and so on.

questions.q: You type 'Mon' into a cell and drag its Fill Handle across. What appears next?
questions.e: Excel recognises weekday names as a built-in series and continues Tue, Wed, and so on.

questions.q: You type Jan-99 and Mar-99 in two cells, select both, and drag the Fill Handle. What comes next?
questions.e: With two starting values 2 months apart, Excel infers a step of 2 months and continues May-99, Jul-99, and so on.

questions.q: In the example above (Jan-99, Mar-99, ...), what does giving Excel two starting values let it determine?
questions.e: Providing two starting values lets Excel calculate the step size (here, 2 months) so it can continue the pattern correctly.

questions.q: In the Series dialog box, which option adds a fixed 'Step value' to each successive cell (e.g. 10, 15, 20...)?
questions.e: The Linear series type adds a fixed step value to each successive cell, producing an arithmetic progression.

questions.q: In the Series dialog box, which option multiplies each successive cell by the step value (e.g. 2, 4, 8, 16...)?
questions.e: The Growth series type multiplies each successive cell by the step value, producing a geometric progression.

questions.q: In the Series dialog box, choosing 'Date' as the series type reveals which extra choice?
questions.e: Choosing Date as the series type reveals a Date unit choice of Day, Weekday, Month or Year, controlling how the date series steps forward.

questions.q: What does holding Ctrl while dragging the Fill Handle do to a single starting number?
o: Nothing changes from the normal fill behaviour
Deletes the value from every filled cell
Forces it to fill as a counting series instead of copying the same value
Converts the number into a text label in each cell
questions.e: Holding Ctrl while dragging a single number's Fill Handle reverses the default behaviour, forcing it to fill as an increasing series instead of repeating the same value.

questions.q: What does holding Ctrl while dragging the Fill Handle do to a recognised series like a custom list or date?
o: Copies the value verbatim instead of continuing the pattern
questions.e: For a recognised series such as a date or custom list, holding Ctrl reverses the default and copies the value verbatim instead of continuing the pattern.

questions.q: Where do you go to create or manage a custom fill series?
o: File > Options > Advanced > Edit Custom Lists
questions.e: Custom fill series are created and managed via File > Options > Advanced > Edit Custom Lists.

questions.q: To turn a range of cells you've already typed (e.g. student names) into a reusable custom list, which button do you use in the Custom Lists dialog?
questions.e: Selecting the existing range and clicking Import in the Custom Lists dialog adds that range as a new custom fill series.

questions.q: To type a brand-new custom list from scratch rather than importing one, what do you select first in the Custom Lists dialog?
questions.e: Choosing NEW LIST in the Custom Lists dialog lets you type each entry of a fresh custom list into the List entries box.

questions.q: After typing your entries for a new custom list in the 'List entries' box, which button saves it?
questions.e: Clicking Add saves the typed entries as a new custom list.

questions.q: If you type one entry from a saved custom list into a cell and drag its Fill Handle to the end of the list and beyond, what happens?
o: The list wraps back to the start and continues
Excel stops filling at the last entry
An error message appears on screen
The list reverses direction and repeats backward
questions.e: Dragging past the last entry of a custom list wraps back to the beginning of the list and continues filling from there.

questions.q: How can an existing custom list be modified later?
o: It cannot be changed once created
Select it in the Custom Lists dialog, edit the entries box, and click Add again
Only by deleting Excel and reinstalling
questions.e: An existing custom list is edited by selecting it in the Custom Lists dialog, changing the entries box, and clicking Add again to save the update.

questions.q: Which symbols can a formula legally begin with in a spreadsheet?
questions.e: A formula may start with =, +, or - (a leading - negates the first term); any other leading symbol is treated as plain text.

questions.q: In the formula -B3+B4, what effect does the leading minus sign have?
o: It negates the value of B3 before adding B4
It deletes the contents of B3
It converts the formula into a comparison
questions.e: A leading minus sign negates the first operand, so the formula effectively computes (-B3)+B4.

questions.q: After you enter a formula and press Enter, what does the cell itself display?
o: The computed result of the formula
Both the formula and the result, stacked
questions.e: The cell shows only the calculated result; the formula text remains visible in the Formula Bar or via F2/double-click.

questions.q: How can you view or edit the formula stored in a cell without deleting its contents?
o: Copy the cell to a blank sheet
Select the cell and press F2, or double-click it
questions.e: F2 (or double-clicking the cell) switches it into in-cell edit mode and highlights every cell the formula references.

questions.q: Which of the following is a valid formula because it uses a built-in function?
questions.e: =COS(20) calls the built-in cosine function on the value 20 — a valid formula component alongside arithmetic and comparison operators.

questions.q: What must be true of a cell before you can type a brand-new formula into it?
o: It must already contain a number
It must be empty, or you intend to overwrite its current contents
It must already be part of a named range
questions.e: A formula is typed into an empty cell (or one being deliberately overwritten); the cell then stores and displays the computed result.

questions.q: The formula =(+B4-B3)/B2 is entered in B5 and then filled across to Z6. What does the formula become in Z6?
questions.e: Relative references shift by the same offset as the destination cell: one row down and from column B to column Z gives =(+Z5-Z4)/Z3.

questions.q: =SUM(B4:D4) is entered in a cell and then copied to cell F5. What does the copied formula read?
questions.e: With purely relative references, the whole range shifts down one row to match the destination row, so B4:D4 becomes B5:D5.

questions.q: A formula =A1+A2 sits in cell C3. It is copied to cell D4. What is the new formula?
questions.e: Copying one column right and one row down shifts every relative reference by (+1 column, +1 row): A1→B2 and A2→B3, giving =B2+B3.

questions.q: By default, when you type a plain cell address like B4 into a formula, what kind of reference is it?
questions.e: Every reference is relative by default unless $ signs are added to make it absolute or mixed.

questions.q: =SUM(A1:A5) is entered in B1 and copied one column right to C1. What does the copy read?
questions.e: Copying one column right shifts a fully relative range one column right: A1:A5 becomes B1:B5.

questions.q: =D2-D1 is entered in D3 and copied two columns right and two rows down, landing in F5. What is the new formula?
questions.e: Shifting +2 columns and +2 rows moves D2→F4 and D1→F3, giving =F4-F3.

questions.q: Which statement about relative references is TRUE?
o: They adjust automatically to preserve their relative position when a formula is copied
They never change, no matter where the formula is copied
They always require a $ sign before the column letter
They only work inside SUM functions
questions.e: That automatic adjustment — keeping the same relative position to the new cell — is exactly what defines a relative reference.

questions.q: What happens to the reference $A$5 when the formula containing it is copied to any other cell?
o: It shifts to match the new cell's row and column
It becomes A5, losing its $ signs
It becomes $A5 only, losing the row lock
questions.e: The $ before both the column and the row locks the reference completely — it never changes when the formula is copied.

questions.q: Pressing F4 repeatedly while a reference is selected cycles through which sequence?
questions.e: F4 cycles a reference through: fully relative → fully absolute → row-absolute/column-relative → column-absolute/row-relative → back to relative.

questions.q: In =SUM(B4:D4)*$D$4, what happens to $D$4 when this formula is copied to a new cell elsewhere on the sheet?
o: It shifts to match the destination cell's row
It shifts to match the destination cell's column
It is dropped from the copied formula entirely
It stays anchored to D4, unchanged
questions.e: Because $D$4 is fully absolute, it stays anchored to D4 in every copy, while the SUM range (relative) adjusts as usual.

questions.q: In the mixed reference $G5, which part is locked (absolute)?
o: Both the column and the row
Neither — it behaves like a relative reference
questions.e: The $ sits directly before the column letter G, so the column is absolute while the row (5) remains relative.

questions.q: In the mixed reference G$5, which part is locked (absolute)?
o: Both the column and the row
Neither — it behaves like a relative reference
questions.e: The $ sits directly before the row number 5, so the row is absolute while the column (G) remains relative.

questions.q: The formula =$A4*B$3 is copied several columns right and several rows down. Which parts of the two references shift?
o: Both the row in $A4 and the column in B$3 stay fixed
The relative row in $A4 and the relative column in B$3 both shift; column A and row 3 stay fixed
Only $A4 changes; B$3 is fully locked
questions.e: $A4 keeps column A fixed but its row shifts with the copy; B$3 keeps row 3 fixed but its column shifts with the copy — that is exactly what a mixed reference does.

questions.q: Which reference form is fully absolute — locked on both the column and the row?
questions.e: A dollar sign before both the column letter and the row number ($A$10) locks the entire reference.

questions.q: Starting from the reference A10 and pressing F4 exactly twice, what form results?
questions.e: F4 press 1: A10 becomes $A$10. F4 press 2: $A$10 becomes A$10. So after two presses the reference reads A$10.

questions.q: Why would you use a mixed reference (like $A4 or B$3) instead of a fully absolute or fully relative one?
o: Mixed references are required by every SUM function
To lock only the row or only the column, e.g. when filling a formula across and down to build a reference grid
Because Excel does not support fully absolute references
questions.e: A mixed reference is useful exactly when you want one axis — row or column — to stay fixed while the other adjusts, such as when building a multiplication-style grid.

questions.q: Entering the formula =(D1+D2-D3)/3 inside cell D3 itself creates what kind of problem?
questions.e: D3's formula depends on D3's own value, so the calculation can never resolve — this is a circular reference, which should be avoided.

questions.q: Are circular references permitted in normal formula use?
o: Yes, and they always resolve to zero
Yes, but only inside IF functions
Yes, but only across different worksheets
No — they should be avoided; the calculation cannot resolve
questions.e: A circular reference makes a cell depend on its own result, so it cannot be computed and should always be corrected.

questions.q: What does the reference Sheet5!A10 mean?
o: Cell A10 on the worksheet named Sheet5
A named range called Sheet5 starting at A10
Row 5, column A10 on the active sheet
questions.e: The sheet name followed by an exclamation mark and a cell address refers to that cell on the named sheet — here, A10 on Sheet5.

questions.q: Which reference correctly points to cell A10 on a worksheet named 'CSM 1' (note the space in the name)?
questions.e: A sheet name containing a space must be wrapped in single quotes, so the correct reference is 'CSM 1'!A10.

questions.q: What does the 3-D reference =SUM(Sheet1:Sheet4!$D$1:$D$10) do?
o: Sums D1:D10 on Sheet1 only, ignoring Sheet4
Sums D1:D10 across Sheet1, Sheet2, Sheet3 and Sheet4 combined
Sums only Sheet1 and Sheet4, skipping the sheets between them
Creates a circular reference across four sheets
questions.e: A 3-D reference spans every sheet from the first named sheet to the last, so this sums D1:D10 on all four sheets, Sheet1 through Sheet4.

questions.q: A worksheet has been renamed to CSM1 (no spaces). Which reference correctly points to cell A10 on it?
questions.e: Single quotes are only required when a sheet name contains a space or other special character; CSM1 has none, so CSM1!A10 is correct as written.

questions.q: Why must a sheet name containing spaces be wrapped in single quotes, as in 'CSM 1'!A10?
o: Because the space would otherwise be read as part of the cell address, breaking the reference
Because sheet names are forbidden from containing spaces at all
Because quotes convert the reference into a text string
Because it turns the reference into a 3-D reference
questions.e: Without quotes, the spreadsheet cannot tell where the sheet name ends and the cell address begins, so a name with a space must be enclosed in single quotes.

questions.q: Which arithmetic operator performs exponentiation in a formula?
questions.e: The caret (^) is the exponentiation operator, e.g. =2^5 raises 2 to the power 5.

questions.q: What is the result of =6/3?
questions.e: Division: 6 divided by 3 equals 2.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the six arithmetic operators (+, –, *, /, %, ^)?
questions.e: & is the text concatenation operator, not an arithmetic one; –, ^ and % are all arithmetic operators.

questions.q: What does the formula ="CSM"&"183" produce?
questions.e: The & operator concatenates (joins) two text strings, combining "CSM" and "183" into "CSM183".

questions.q: What do all six comparison operators (=, >, =, ) have in common?
o: They always return TRUE or FALSE
They can only be used with text values
They require the & operator to work
questions.e: Comparison (relational) operators compare two values and always return the logical value TRUE or FALSE.

questions.q: Which comparison operator means 'not equal to'?
questions.e: The 'not equal to' operator is written <>, not !=. For example, =A1<>B1 returns TRUE when A1 and B1 differ.

questions.q: The reference A10:G40 uses which reference operator, and what does it do?
o: The union operator, combining two separate ranges
The intersection operator, finding cells common to two ranges
The concatenation operator, joining two addresses
The range operator, producing one reference to every cell between A10 and G40, inclusive
questions.e: The colon (:) is the range, or 'to', operator — A10:G40 means every cell from A10 to G40 inclusive.

questions.q: What does the reference operator comma (,) do, as in MAX(B15,B19:G15)?
o: It unions separate references into one, non-contiguous reference
It finds cells common to both ranges
It multiplies the two ranges together
questions.e: The comma is the union, or 'and', operator — it combines multiple references, here cell B15 and the range B19:G15, into one reference for the function to evaluate.

questions.q: What does the intersection (space) reference operator return when the two ranges share no common cells?
questions.e: When two ranges combined with the space (intersection) operator share no cells in common, the spreadsheet returns the #NULL! error.

questions.q: Which comparison operator would you use to test whether a value is 'greater than or equal to' another?
questions.e: 'Greater than or equal to' is written >=, with the equals sign after the greater-than sign.

questions.q: What is the result of =8/2^3?
questions.e: Exponentiation outranks division: 2^3 = 8 first, then 8/8 = 1.

questions.q: What is the result of =10/(5*2)?
questions.e: Parentheses are evaluated first: 5×2 = 10, then 10/10 = 1.

questions.q: What is the result of =2+3*4?
questions.e: Multiplication outranks addition: 3×4 = 12 first, then 2+12 = 14.

questions.q: What is the result of =-2^2, where negation is applied to 2 before the power is taken?
questions.e: Negation has higher precedence than exponentiation, so the negative sign applies first: (-2)^2 = 4.

questions.q: What is the result of =100/10/2?
questions.e: Division is evaluated left to right when operators share the same precedence: 100/10 = 10, then 10/2 = 5.

questions.q: Which of the following is a VALID name for a cell range, following the naming rules?
questions.e: A name must start with a letter or underscore — _Sales2024 is valid. 2024_Sales starts with a digit, Unit-Price has a hyphen, and Total Sales has a space, all of which are disallowed.

questions.q: Which characters are NOT allowed anywhere in a defined name?
questions.e: Defined names cannot contain spaces or hyphens; they may contain letters, digits (not as the first character) and underscores.

questions.q: What is the maximum length allowed for a defined name?
questions.e: A defined name may be up to 255 characters long.

questions.q: Are defined names case-sensitive?
o: Yes — 'Sales' and 'sales' are treated as different names
No — 'Sales', 'SALES' and 'sales' all refer to the same name
Only the first letter's case matters
Case sensitivity depends on the workbook's language setting
questions.e: Defined names are not case-sensitive, so Sales, SALES and sales all point to the same defined name.

questions.q: In the New Name dialog (Formulas tab → Define Name), which three fields are provided?
questions.e: The New Name dialog has a Name field, an optional Comment field, and a Refers To field showing the address the name points to.

questions.q: What is the Name Manager, on the Formulas tab, primarily used for?
o: Sorting a range of names alphabetically
Creating, editing or deleting several defined names in one session
questions.e: The Name Manager gives a central place to view and manage every defined name in the workbook, useful when several names need to be created or edited at once.

questions.q: What is a 'function' in Excel?
o: A predefined, built-in formula supplied by Excel
A chart type used to display formulas
A macro written entirely by the user in VBA
A keyboard shortcut for formatting cells
questions.e: A function is a predefined, built-in formula that performs a specific calculation using the values (arguments) you supply.

questions.q: Why is =SUM(A1:A1000) preferred over manually typing 1000 additions?
o: It only works on whole numbers
It reduces typographical errors, is faster, and needs far fewer keystrokes
It produces a different total each time
Excel requires functions for ranges larger than 10 cells
questions.e: Built-in functions cut down on typing, speed up processing, and greatly reduce the risk of typographical errors compared with a manually typed chain of additions.

questions.q: In the formula =ROUND(A1,2), what is 'ROUND'?
questions.e: ROUND is the function name; A1 and 2 are its two arguments, separated by a comma.

questions.q: What always encloses a function's arguments?
questions.e: Arguments always follow the function name inside a pair of parentheses, even when there are none, e.g. NOW().

questions.q: Which of these can NOT be used as a function argument?
o: A cell reference such as A1
A nested function such as SUM
questions.e: Arguments may be constants, cell references, or nested functions — a worksheet tab's color is not a valid argument type.

questions.q: RAND(), PI() and NOW() belong to which class of functions?
questions.e: These functions take no arguments at all, though the empty parentheses are still required.

questions.q: ROUNDDOWN() always requires exactly two arguments. Which class of function is this?
questions.e: A fixed-argument function always needs the same, unchanging number of arguments — ROUNDDOWN always needs a number and a digit count.

questions.q: Where in Excel's ribbon do you find the Insert Function dialog and the full set of function categories?
questions.e: The Formulas tab hosts the Insert Function (fx) button and the function library, organised by category.

questions.q: After choosing a category and a function in the Insert Function dialog, what opens next?
o: The Function Arguments dialog, prompting for each argument
questions.e: Excel opens the Function Arguments dialog so you can fill in each required and optional argument, with a live preview of the result.

questions.q: Clicking the small arrow beside the AutoSum button reveals which additional options?
questions.e: Besides the default Sum, the AutoSum dropdown offers Average, Count Numbers, Max and Min for the adjacent range.

questions.q: Which category retrieves data from records in a list or database that meet given criteria?
questions.e: The Database category performs calculations, such as sums and averages, on records meeting given criteria.

questions.q: Which category is kept mainly for compatibility with older Excel versions' statistical function names?
questions.e: The Compatibility category preserves older statistical function names so worksheets built in earlier Excel versions still work correctly.

questions.q: What does NOW() return?
o: The current date and time together
A count of business days remaining this month
questions.e: NOW() is a no-argument function returning both the current date and time as a serial number.

questions.q: How does TODAY() differ from NOW()?
o: TODAY returns only the time, with no date portion
TODAY returns only the date, with no time portion
TODAY requires an argument, NOW does not
questions.e: TODAY() returns only the current date's serial number, while NOW() returns both date and time.

questions.q: What does =DATE(2010,9,28) return internally?
o: An error, since day must come before year
The serial number 40450 for that date
The value TRUE displayed in the cell
questions.e: DATE(year,month,day) returns Excel's internal serial number for that date — 40450 for 28 September 2010.

questions.q: Which function converts a date stored as text into a serial number?
questions.e: DATEVALUE(text) converts text that looks like a date into the equivalent date serial number.

questions.q: Which function returns the number of whole working days between two dates, excluding weekends?
questions.e: NETWORKDAYS(start,end) counts whole working days between two dates, excluding Saturdays and Sundays.

questions.q: Which function returns a date that is a given number of working days after a start date?
questions.e: WORKDAY(start,days) returns the date that is a given number of working days before or after a start date.

questions.q: Which function returns the last day of the month, a given number of months from a start date?
questions.e: EOMONTH(start,months) returns the last day of the month a given number of months before or after the start date.

questions.q: Which function extracts the day-of-the-week as a number from a date?
questions.e: WEEKDAY(serial) returns a number representing the day of the week for a given date.

questions.q: Excel's trig functions such as SIN and COS expect angles in which unit?
questions.e: Excel's trigonometric functions expect radians; use RADIANS() to convert degrees to radians first.

questions.q: Which function converts an angle from radians back to degrees?
questions.e: DEGREES(angle) converts a radian value into degrees; RADIANS() does the reverse conversion.

questions.q: What does =INT(7.9) return?
questions.e: INT() rounds a number down to the nearest integer, so INT(7.9) = 7 (unlike ROUND, which would give 8).

questions.q: Which function returns a random integer between two given numbers?
questions.e: RANDBETWEEN(bottom,top) returns a random integer in the given range; RAND() instead returns a random decimal between 0 and 1 with no arguments.

questions.q: What does =SUMIF(A1:A10,">50") do?
o: Sums every cell in A1:A10 regardless of value
Counts the cells in A1:A10 that are greater than 50
Sums only the cells in A1:A10 that are greater than 50
questions.e: SUMIF adds only the cells in the range that meet the given condition — here, values greater than 50.

questions.q: Given the values 4, 8, 6, 2, 10 in A1:A5, what does =MAX(A1:A5) return?
questions.e: MAX() returns the largest value in the set, which is 10.

questions.q: Which function returns the k-th largest value in a data set?
questions.e: LARGE(array,k) returns the k-th largest value; SMALL() does the equivalent for the smallest values.

questions.q: Which function counts cells in a range that meet a single given condition?
questions.e: COUNTIF(range,criteria) counts the cells in a range that satisfy one condition, e.g. COUNTIF(A1:A10,">60").

questions.q: Which function returns the correlation coefficient between two data sets?
questions.e: CORREL(array1,array2) measures the strength and direction of the linear relationship between two data sets.

questions.q: What does =LEFT("Excel",3) return?
questions.e: LEFT(text,num_chars) returns characters from the start of the string, so LEFT("Excel",3) = "Exc".

questions.q: What does =UPPER("knust") return?
questions.e: UPPER() converts every letter in the text to uppercase, giving "KNUST".

questions.q: What does =CONCATENATE("CSM"," ","177") return?
questions.e: CONCATENATE joins the given text strings end to end in order: "CSM" + " " + "177" = "CSM 177".

questions.q: Which function removes extra spaces from text, leaving single spaces between words?
questions.e: TRIM(text) strips leading, trailing, and repeated internal spaces, leaving single spaces between words.

questions.q: Which function returns characters extracted from the middle of a text string?
questions.e: MID() extracts a given number of characters starting from a specified position within the text.

questions.q: Which function checks whether two text strings are identical, including case?
questions.e: EXACT(text1,text2) performs a case-sensitive comparison and returns TRUE only if the strings match exactly.

questions.q: In financial functions, what does the argument 'nper' represent?
o: The total number of payment periods
The present value of the investment
questions.e: 'nper' is the total number of payment periods over the life of the loan or investment.

questions.q: In financial functions, what does 'type' = 1 mean?
o: Payments are due at the end of each period
Payments are due at the start of each period
questions.e: type = 1 means payments are made in advance (start of period); type = 0 (the default) means arrears (end of period).

questions.q: By Excel's sign convention for financial functions, what does a negative value represent?
o: A future value of exactly zero
Cash paid out of your account
questions.e: Negative values represent cash paid out of your pocket (e.g. a deposit or loan payment); positive values represent cash received.

questions.q: Which function calculates the periodic payment required to repay a loan?
questions.e: PMT(rate,nper,pv,fv,type) returns the fixed periodic payment for a loan or annuity.

questions.q: Which function calculates the future value of a series of regular, constant payments?
questions.e: FV(rate,nper,pmt,pv,type) returns the future value an investment grows to given regular payments.

questions.q: Evaluating =PMT(12%/12,60,-1000000.00) — what is this formula modelling?
o: The future value of a savings account after 60 years
The present value of 60 equal deposits
The monthly repayment on a 1,000,000 loan at 12% annual interest over 60 months
The annual interest rate on a 5-year loan
questions.e: 12%/12 is the monthly rate, 60 is the number of monthly periods, and -1,000,000 is the loan's present value; PMT returns the required monthly repayment (≈22,244).

questions.q: Evaluating =FV(10%/12,15*12,-200000) — what does 15*12 represent?
o: The present value of the account
The total number of monthly periods
questions.e: 15*12 converts 15 years into 180 monthly periods, matching the monthly rate 10%/12 used elsewhere in the formula.

questions.q: Which function calculates straight-line depreciation for one period?
questions.e: SLN(cost,salvage,life) returns straight-line depreciation, spreading the depreciable amount evenly across the asset's life.

questions.q: Which function returns the internal rate of return for a series of cash flows?
questions.e: IRR(values) calculates the discount rate at which the net present value of the cash flows equals zero.

questions.q: What does =AND(TRUE,TRUE,FALSE) return?
questions.e: AND() returns TRUE only when every argument is TRUE; since one argument is FALSE here, the result is FALSE.

questions.q: What does =OR(FALSE,FALSE,TRUE) return?
questions.e: OR() returns TRUE if any argument is TRUE; since one argument here is TRUE, the overall result is TRUE.

questions.q: Given F1 = 45 hours worked, what does =IF(F1>40,(F1-40)*1.5,0) return?
questions.e: Since 45 > 40, the TRUE branch runs: (45-40)*1.5 = 5*1.5 = 7.5 overtime-hours-equivalent pay multiplier.

questions.q: For the nested formula =IF(A1>=1000,0.15,IF(A1>=500,0.10,IF(A1>=100,0.05,0))), what discount applies when A1 = 650?
questions.e: 650 is not ≥1000, so Excel checks the next condition: 650 is ≥500, so the 10% branch applies.

questions.q: What does NOT(TRUE) return?
questions.e: NOT() reverses its argument's logical value, so NOT(TRUE) returns FALSE.

questions.q: Which function searches for a value in the first column of a table and returns a value from a column to the right?
questions.e: VLOOKUP(value,table,col_index) searches vertically down the first column of a table for a match, then returns a value from a specified column.

questions.q: Which function returns the relative position of an item within an array that matches a specified value?
questions.e: MATCH(value,array,match_type) returns the position of the matching item, which is often fed into INDEX() to retrieve a related value.

questions.q: Which function searches for a value in the top row of a table and returns a value from a row below it?
questions.e: HLOOKUP(value,table,row_index) works like VLOOKUP but searches horizontally across the top row of a table.

questions.q: Which function converts a vertical range of cells into a horizontal one, and vice versa?
questions.e: TRANSPOSE(array) flips the orientation of a range, turning rows into columns or columns into rows.

questions.q: Which ribbon path applies a preset table style (AutoFormat) to a selected range?
questions.e: AutoFormat's preset table styles are applied via Home > Format as Table in the Style group.

questions.q: How can you preview an AutoFormat table style before applying it?
o: Hover the mouse over a style thumbnail
Press F5 to refresh the gallery
Open Print Preview from the File tab
questions.e: Hovering over a thumbnail in the Format as Table gallery shows a live preview on the worksheet before you click to apply it.

questions.q: What does the Format Painter copy from a source cell to a destination cell?
questions.e: Format Painter copies the complete set of formatting (font, borders, shading, number format, etc.) from the source cell.

questions.q: You need to paste the same format onto five scattered, non-adjacent cells. What should you do?
o: Single-click Format Painter five separate times
Hold Shift and click Format Painter each time
Use Ctrl+P repeatedly to reprint formatting
Double-click Format Painter, then click each destination, then press Esc
questions.e: Double-clicking Format Painter keeps it active for multiple destinations; press Esc to turn it off when done.

questions.q: After using Format Painter with a single click on one destination cell, what happens?
o: It switches off after that one paste
It stays active for further clicks
It opens the Format Cells dialog
questions.e: A single click on Format Painter copies the format once, then the tool deactivates automatically.

questions.q: How do you exit Format Painter after double-clicking it to paste to multiple destinations?
questions.e: Pressing Esc (or clicking the Format Painter button again) releases it after multi-destination use.

questions.q: To make only one word bold inside a longer sentence typed in a single cell, you should first do what?
o: Select the whole cell and apply bold
Split the cell into two cells
Highlight just that word in the formula bar or edit mode, then apply bold
questions.e: Character-level formatting requires highlighting only the target characters (via the formula bar or in-cell edit mode) before applying the style.

questions.q: Which dialog gives full control over character formatting (font, style, size, effects) for a selection?
questions.e: The Format Cells dialog's Font tab provides complete control over character formatting.

questions.q: What is the keyboard shortcut for Bold in Excel?
questions.e: Bold can be toggled with either Ctrl+2 or Ctrl+B.

questions.q: What is the keyboard shortcut for Italic in Excel?
questions.e: Italic can be toggled with either Ctrl+3 or Ctrl+I.

questions.q: What is the keyboard shortcut for Underline in Excel?
questions.e: Underline can be toggled with either Ctrl+4 or Ctrl+U.

questions.q: What is the keyboard shortcut for Strikethrough in Excel?
questions.e: Strikethrough is toggled with Ctrl+5.

questions.q: Which shortcut toggles Bold formatting using a number key combination (not a letter)?
questions.e: Ctrl+2 is the numeric-key alternative to Ctrl+B for Bold.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of Excel's formatting shortcut keys?
questions.e: Strikethrough is Ctrl+5, not Ctrl+6 — the four shortcuts are Ctrl+2, Ctrl+3, Ctrl+4 and Ctrl+5.

questions.q: Font size is measured in which unit?
questions.e: Font sizes are measured in points, where 1 inch equals 72 points.

questions.q: How many points make up one inch?
questions.e: By the standard typographic measurement, 1 inch = 72 points.

questions.q: Which of these is one of the basic font styles available in Excel?
questions.e: Excel's basic character styles are plain (regular), bold, italic and underline, which can also be combined.

questions.q: Approximately how many different fonts can a single Excel worksheet support?
questions.e: Excel supports up to 256 fonts on a single worksheet, though using too many is poor design practice.

questions.q: A worksheet uses 300 distinct fonts. What is the issue?
o: This is fine, there is no limit
Excel will auto-convert them all to Calibri
This exceeds Excel's supported limit of 256 fonts per worksheet
questions.e: Excel supports a maximum of 256 fonts per worksheet, so 300 distinct fonts would exceed that limit.

questions.q: Which button both combines selected cells into one and horizontally centers the content?
questions.e: Merge and Center (Home > Alignment) merges the selected cells into one and centers the text across them.

questions.q: You want text to appear centered across several columns for a title, but you need each underlying cell to remain separate (not merged). Which option should you use?
questions.e: Center Across Selection, found under Format Cells > Alignment tab > Horizontal dropdown, visually centers text without merging the cells.

questions.q: Where is the option to set Horizontal alignment to 'Center Across Selection' found?
o: Format Cells dialog > Alignment tab > Horizontal dropdown
questions.e: The Horizontal dropdown on the Alignment tab of Format Cells includes 'Center Across Selection' as an option.

questions.q: What is the key functional difference between Merge and Center and Merge Across Selection?
o: Merge Across Selection only works on rows
Merge and Center actually merges the cells; Center Across Selection only visually centers text without merging them
Merge and Center cannot be undone
questions.e: Merge and Center physically combines the cells into one; Center Across Selection keeps the individual cells intact and only shifts the visual display.

questions.q: A cell contains a long sentence that overflows into neighboring blank cells. Which command makes the text wrap onto multiple lines within the same cell instead?
questions.e: Wrap Text forces long content to wrap onto multiple lines inside the cell, automatically increasing row height to fit.

questions.q: Where can you find the Wrap Text checkbox besides the ribbon button?
questions.e: Wrap Text is available both as a ribbon button and as a checkbox on the Alignment tab of Format Cells.

questions.q: What happens to row height when Wrap Text causes a cell's content to span three lines?
o: Row height stays fixed and content is clipped
Row height automatically increases to show all wrapped lines
The column width automatically increases instead
questions.e: Wrap Text automatically increases the row height so every wrapped line remains visible, without the user manually adjusting the row height.

questions.q: Which checkbox, found in the Alignment tab of Format Cells, physically combines a selected range into a single cell?
questions.e: The Merge Cells checkbox on the Alignment tab combines the selected cells into one.

questions.q: Which operator is used in Excel formulas to join (concatenate) text and numbers together?
questions.e: The ampersand (&) operator joins text strings, cell references and function results into one combined string.

questions.q: Cell B12 contains the text 'Final Sales for' and cell C12 contains the number 1999. What does =B12&TEXT(C12,"####") return?
questions.e: The formula concatenates B12's text directly with C12's number formatted as ####, producing 'Final Sales for1999' with no automatic space.

questions.q: Why does =B12&TEXT(C12,"####") NOT include a space between the text and the number?
o: Excel always inserts a space automatically
The & operator joins strings exactly as given, with no automatic spacing
TEXT removes any spaces from its result
B12 must contain a trailing space by default
questions.e: The & operator simply concatenates the exact strings provided; any spacing must be added explicitly, e.g. with &" "&.

questions.q: What is the role of the TEXT() function inside a concatenation formula like =B12&TEXT(C12,"####")?
o: It converts a number into a formatted text string for display
It converts text into a number
questions.e: TEXT() converts a numeric value into a text string using a specified format code, which can then be safely concatenated.

questions.q: To join B12's text with C12's number AND include a space between them, which formula is correct?
questions.e: Adding &" "& between the two parts inserts a literal space character in the concatenated result.

questions.q: If you type $12.95 into a blank cell, what does Excel automatically apply?
questions.e: Excel recognizes the dollar sign and decimal places and automatically applies Currency format.

questions.q: You type 15% into a cell. What does the formula bar show when that cell is selected?
questions.e: Although the cell displays '15%', the underlying stored value shown in the formula bar is the decimal 0.15.

questions.q: After typing 15%, the cell displays '15%' on the worksheet. What is actually stored and used in calculations?
questions.e: Percentage format multiplies the stored decimal by 100 for display; the true stored value remains 0.15.

questions.q: Typing $12.95 applies Currency automatically. What underlying value does Excel store for that cell?
questions.e: Excel stores the numeric value 12.95 and simply displays it with a currency symbol and two decimals.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the three ways to apply a number format described in this module?
o: The Number Format dropdown on the ribbon
questions.e: Dragging the column border adjusts column width, not number formatting. The three number-format methods are the ribbon dropdown, Format Cells dialog, and shortcut keys.

questions.q: Which ribbon tab and group houses the Number Format dropdown?
questions.e: The Number Format dropdown sits in the Number group on the Home tab.

questions.q: Which tab of the Format Cells dialog controls number formats such as Currency, Percentage and Date?
questions.e: The Number tab of Format Cells contains every built-in number format category and their options.

questions.q: What is the shortcut key for applying General format?
questions.e: Ctrl+Shift+~ (tilde) removes special number formatting, returning a cell to General.

questions.q: What is the shortcut key for applying Number format with two decimal places?
questions.e: Ctrl+Shift+! applies Number format with two decimal places and a thousands separator.

questions.q: What is the shortcut key for applying Currency format?
questions.e: Ctrl+Shift+$ applies Currency format, adding the currency symbol and two decimals.

questions.q: What is the shortcut key for applying Percent format?
questions.e: Ctrl+Shift+% applies Percentage format, multiplying the value by 100 and adding a % sign.

questions.q: What is the shortcut key for applying Scientific format?
questions.e: Ctrl+Shift+^ applies Scientific notation (E+n) to the selected cell.

questions.q: Which pair correctly matches a shortcut to its format?
questions.e: Ctrl+Shift+^ correctly applies Scientific format; the other pairings in this question are mismatched.

questions.q: Which number format category is Excel's default and switches to scientific notation for very large numbers (about 12+ digits)?
questions.e: General is Excel's default format; it has no specific style and shifts to scientific notation once a number gets too large to display normally.

questions.q: Which format category is best suited for general monetary values, adding a currency symbol placed directly next to the digits?
questions.e: Currency format adds the default currency symbol immediately beside the number's digits.

questions.q: Which number format category aligns BOTH the currency symbols AND the decimal points down a column of figures?
questions.e: Accounting format's defining feature is that it lines up currency symbols at the left and decimal points on the right, unlike plain Currency format.

questions.q: What is the main visual difference between Currency and Accounting formats?
o: Accounting aligns currency symbols and decimal points in a column; Currency places the symbol right against the digits
Currency aligns symbols and decimals; Accounting does not
questions.e: Accounting neatly aligns symbols and decimals down the column (ledger style), whereas Currency places the symbol directly beside each number's digits.

questions.q: Which format category would you use to display a cell as 'ZIP code' or 'Social Security number' style data?
questions.e: Special format is designed for list/database values like ZIP codes, phone numbers and Social Security numbers.

questions.q: Which format category displays a number using E+n exponential notation?
questions.e: Scientific format replaces part of a number's display with exponential E+n notation.

questions.q: Which format category displays a decimal value as a fraction, e.g. 1/2 instead of 0.5?
questions.e: Fraction format converts and displays a decimal value in fractional form with a chosen denominator precision.

questions.q: Which format category forces the cell's content to be treated and displayed exactly as typed, even if it looks numeric?
questions.e: Text format displays content exactly as entered (e.g. keeping a leading zero like '007'), rather than interpreting it as a number.

questions.q: Which format category multiplies the cell's stored value by 100 and appends a % symbol?
questions.e: Percentage format multiplies the underlying decimal value by 100 for display and adds the % sign.

questions.q: Roughly how many custom number formats does Excel allow a user to define in a workbook?
questions.e: Excel typically allows between 200 and 250 custom formats per workbook, depending on the language version.

questions.q: Which format category's built-in formats, marked with an asterisk (*), respond automatically to the Windows Control Panel's regional date/time settings?
questions.e: Asterisk-marked Date/Time formats automatically adjust display style based on the regional settings configured in Control Panel.

questions.q: Which category would you choose to define your own format code, such as displaying a number followed by the text 'kg'?
questions.e: Custom format lets a user build a personal format code, such as 0.00 "kg", by editing an existing built-in format.

questions.q: How do you manually resize a column using the mouse?
o: Double-click any cell in the column
Drag the border between two column headers
questions.e: Dragging the border between two column headers, where the pointer becomes a double-headed arrow, resizes that column.

questions.q: What happens when you double-click the border between two column headers?
o: The column AutoFits to the width of its widest entry
questions.e: Double-clicking a column-header border triggers AutoFit, resizing the column to match its widest content.

questions.q: Which ribbon path lets you type an exact numeric column width value?
questions.e: Home > Format > Column Width opens a dialog where an exact width value can be entered.

questions.q: What is generally the first step in the printing workflow for a large worksheet?
o: Select the range to be printed
questions.e: Before anything else, you select the range/area you actually want printed, then move on to previewing page breaks and adjusting Page Setup.

questions.q: Which view lets you see exactly where automatic page breaks will fall before printing?
questions.e: View > Page Break Preview shows the page divisions as dashed (automatic) or solid (manual) lines directly over the worksheet.

questions.q: After previewing page breaks and making any manual adjustments, what is the next typical step?
o: Open File > Print and select a printer
Turn off AutoSave in the settings
questions.e: Once breaks look right, you go to File > Print, choose the correct printer, then fine-tune via Page Setup before the final Print Preview.

questions.q: Where can the Page Setup dialog be opened from, besides File > Page Setup?
o: The Page Setup button inside Print Preview
The status bar zoom slider control
The Name Box beside the Formula bar
The Formula bar above the grid
questions.e: Print Preview includes its own Page Setup button, letting you adjust settings without leaving the preview screen.

questions.q: How many tabs does the Page Setup dialog have?
questions.e: The Page Setup dialog has four tabs: Page, Margins, Header/Footer and Sheet.

questions.q: Which tab of Page Setup controls paper size and orientation?
questions.e: The Page tab holds orientation, paper size, print quality and scaling (Adjust To / Fit To) options.

questions.q: Which tab of Page Setup controls the print area and print titles?
questions.e: The Sheet tab contains the Print Area box, Print Titles (rows/columns to repeat), gridlines, and page order settings.

questions.q: Which tab of Page Setup lets you centre the printout horizontally and vertically on the page?
questions.e: The Margins tab has 'Center on page' checkboxes for Horizontally and Vertically, along with the margin size fields.

questions.q: Which tab of Page Setup is used to build a custom footer with page numbers?
questions.e: The Header/Footer tab offers predefined formats and the Custom Header/Custom Footer dialogs for building your own.

questions.q: Which orientation prints the page wider than it is tall?
questions.e: Landscape orientation turns the page on its side, making it wider than tall — useful for worksheets with many columns.

questions.q: Portrait orientation is best suited to worksheets that have:
questions.e: Portrait prints taller than wide, which fits worksheets with many rows better than ones with many columns.

questions.q: On the Page tab, what does 'print quality' typically refer to?
questions.e: Print quality on the Page tab sets the resolution (dots per inch) the printer will use, affecting sharpness and speed.

questions.q: Where do you choose between standard paper sizes such as Letter, A4 and Legal?
questions.e: Paper size is selected from a dropdown on the Page tab, alongside orientation and scaling.

questions.q: Which scaling option lets you shrink or enlarge the printout by a specific percentage?
questions.e: Adjust To scales the print by a chosen percentage of normal size, e.g. 75% or 120%.
questions.t: Scaling: Adjust To vs Fit To

questions.q: Which scaling option lets you specify the exact number of pages wide and tall the printout should occupy?
questions.e: Fit To automatically calculates the scale percentage needed so the printout fits, e.g., 1 page wide by 2 pages tall.
questions.t: Scaling: Adjust To vs Fit To

questions.q: Both Adjust To and Fit To scaling require the printer to support:
questions.e: Scaling relies on the printer's ability to render fonts at arbitrary sizes, which requires scalable/TrueType font support.
questions.t: Scaling: Adjust To vs Fit To

questions.q: You want a wide worksheet to print on exactly 1 page wide by 3 pages tall. Which option should you use?
o: Fit To 1 page wide by 3 tall
questions.e: Fit To directly specifies the page dimensions of the printout, which is exactly this requirement.
questions.t: Scaling: Adjust To vs Fit To

questions.q: What is the default top and bottom margin, in inches?
questions.e: The default top and bottom margins are 1.0 inch each in the Margins tab of Page Setup.

questions.q: What is the default left and right margin, in inches?
questions.e: The default left and right margins are 0.75 inch each, smaller than the top/bottom defaults.

questions.q: Which checkbox centres the print area evenly between the left and right margins?
questions.e: The 'Horizontally' checkbox on the Margins tab centres the data left-to-right on the page.

questions.q: Which checkbox centres the print area evenly between the top and bottom margins?
questions.e: The 'Vertically' checkbox on the Margins tab centres the data top-to-bottom on the page.

questions.q: Why does the Margins tab include a small preview area?
o: To give a live visual of margin and centering changes
To show print quality in dpi
To display the print area's named range
questions.e: A miniature live preview lets you see how margin and centering adjustments affect the page layout before printing.

questions.q: If both the Horizontally and Vertically checkboxes are checked for a small print area, where will the data appear on the page?
o: In the top-left corner of the page
Centred in the middle of the page
In the bottom-right corner of the page
questions.e: Checking both centring options places the data in the middle of the page rather than flush to a corner.

questions.q: By default, do worksheet gridlines print on the page?
o: No, unless the Gridlines box on the Sheet tab is checked
Only if Draft Quality mode is turned on
Yes, gridlines always print by default
Only when Landscape mode is selected
questions.e: On-screen gridlines are not printed by default; you must check the Gridlines box on the Sheet tab to include them.

questions.q: Which Page Setup tab has the checkbox to print row numbers and column letters?
questions.e: The Sheet tab's Row and Column Headings checkbox controls whether the 1,2,3 / A,B,C headings print.

questions.q: Turning off gridlines for on-screen display is done through:
questions.e: On-screen gridline visibility is a separate setting, found in Tools/Options (or the View ribbon) — it does not affect printing.

questions.q: Which Sheet tab option forces a colour worksheet to print without colour?
questions.e: The Black and White checkbox forces the printout to render without colour, even on a colour printer.

questions.q: What is the Sheet tab option that decides whether pages are numbered down-then-across or across-then-down called?
questions.e: The Page Order option offers 'Down, then Over' and 'Over, then Down' choices for numbering multi-page printouts.

questions.q: 'Down, Then Over' page order means pages are numbered:
o: Across the first row of pages, then down
Down the first column of pages, then across to the next column
questions.e: Down, Then Over numbers pages going down through the first set of columns before moving to the next set of columns.

questions.q: 'Over, Then Down' page order means pages are numbered:
o: Across the first row of pages, then down to the next row
Only when print titles are set
Down the first column, then across
questions.e: Over, Then Down numbers pages across the first set of rows before moving down to the next set of rows.

questions.q: Which Page Setup tab contains the Print Area box?
questions.e: The Print Area box, used to limit printing to a chosen range, is on the Sheet tab.

questions.q: What button lets you shrink the Page Setup dialog to more easily select cells for the Print Area box?
questions.e: The Collapse Dialog button minimises the dialog out of the way so you can drag-select the desired range on the sheet.

questions.q: How do you separate multiple print area ranges typed into the Print Area box?
questions.e: Multiple ranges in the Print Area box are separated by commas, e.g. A1:D10,F1:H20, and print in the order listed.

questions.q: Setting a print area automatically creates a named range called:
questions.e: The program automatically defines a named range called Print_Area for whichever range you set as the print area.

questions.q: Which menu path clears a previously set print area?
o: File > Print Area > Clear Print Area
questions.e: File > Print Area > Clear Print Area removes the defined print area, making the whole used range printable again.

questions.q: Besides using File > Print Area > Clear Print Area, how else can you remove a print area?
o: Restart the program and reopen the file
Change the paper size in Page Setup
Delete/clear the text in the Print Area box on the Sheet tab
questions.e: Simply clearing the text entered into the Print Area box on the Sheet tab also removes the print area.

questions.q: If a worksheet has no print area set, what gets printed by default?
o: Nothing at all gets sent to the printer
The entire used range of the worksheet
questions.e: Without a defined print area, printing defaults to the worksheet's entire used range.

questions.q: Print Titles are used for:
o: Naming the printer used for the job
Choosing the paper size and orientation
Repeating a header row or label column on every printed page
Setting the file name in the footer
questions.e: Print Titles let you designate rows to repeat at the top or columns to repeat at the left, so headings appear on every page of a multi-page printout.

questions.q: Where are the 'Rows to Repeat at Top' and 'Columns to Repeat at Left' boxes found?
questions.e: These boxes are part of the Print Titles section on the Sheet tab of Page Setup.

questions.q: Why would you set a Print Titles row when printing a 10-page report?
o: So the column headings reprint at the top of every page for readability
To change the paper size on every page
questions.e: Repeating the header row via Print Titles keeps column labels visible on every page, without requiring a scroll back to page 1.

questions.q: To insert a manual vertical page break, where should the active cell be positioned?
o: Column A of the target row
Any cell in the print area
The last cell of the worksheet
questions.e: A vertical page break is inserted by placing the active cell in row 1 of the column where the new page should begin, then choosing Insert > Page Break.

questions.q: To insert a manual horizontal page break, where should the active cell be positioned?
o: The top-left cell of the sheet
Column A of the target row
questions.e: A horizontal page break is inserted by placing the active cell in column A of the row where the new page should begin, then choosing Insert > Page Break.

questions.q: If the active cell is neither in row 1 nor in column A when you choose Insert > Page Break, what happens?
o: Only a vertical break is inserted
Only a horizontal break is inserted
Both a vertical and a horizontal break are inserted
Nothing is inserted at the active cell
questions.e: When the active cell sits away from row 1 and column A, Insert > Page Break inserts a vertical break to its left and a horizontal break above it simultaneously.

questions.q: How do you remove all manual page breaks from a worksheet at once?
o: Select the entire worksheet, then Insert > Reset All Page Breaks
Switch to Print Preview and check pages
Delete every row on the worksheet
Change the paper size in Page Setup
questions.e: Selecting the whole worksheet and choosing Reset All Page Breaks (or Remove All Page Breaks) clears every manual break in one step.

questions.q: How do you remove a single manual page break?
o: Click a cell adjacent to the break, then Insert > Remove Page Break
Reset All Page Breaks at once
questions.e: Selecting a cell just below or to the right of the break and choosing Remove Page Break deletes only that one break.

questions.q: In Page Break Preview, how are manual page breaks typically distinguished from automatic ones?
o: Manual breaks are solid lines, automatic breaks are dashed
Manual breaks are red, automatic are green
Manual breaks only appear in Landscape mode
questions.e: Automatic breaks appear as dashed lines while manual (user-inserted) breaks appear as solid lines in Page Break Preview.

questions.q: What happens if you drag an automatic page break line in Page Break Preview?
o: Nothing — automatic breaks cannot be moved
It converts into a manual page break
questions.e: Dragging an automatic (dashed) break to a new position converts it into a fixed manual (solid) break.

questions.q: Which Page Setup tab is used to add headers and footers?
questions.e: The Header/Footer tab offers predefined formats plus Custom Header/Custom Footer dialogs.

questions.q: What are the three sections available in the Custom Header/Custom Footer dialog?
questions.e: Custom headers and footers each have a Left, Center and Right section that align text accordingly on the page.

questions.q: Which keyboard shortcut jumps to the Left section of the Custom Header/Footer dialog?
questions.e: Alt+L moves focus to the Left section box, Alt+C to Center, and Alt+R to Right.

questions.q: Which keyboard shortcut jumps to the Center section of the Custom Header/Footer dialog?
questions.e: Alt+C moves focus directly to the Center section of the header/footer dialog.

questions.q: Which keyboard shortcut jumps to the Right section of the Custom Header/Footer dialog?
questions.e: Alt+R moves focus to the Right section, commonly used for page numbers or dates.

questions.q: Which shortcut inserts a line break so a header or footer section can hold multiple lines?
questions.e: Alt+Enter inserts a line break within a header/footer section, allowing multi-line text such as a title on one line and a date on the next.

questions.q: Besides typing free text, how else can you add content to a header/footer section?
o: Using toolbar buttons for codes like page number, date, file name and sheet name
Only by pasting from another program
questions.e: The Custom Header/Footer dialog provides toolbar buttons that insert dynamic codes such as page number, total pages, date, time, file name, sheet name and a picture.

questions.q: Which menu command opens Print Preview?
questions.e: File > Print Preview (or the Preview button from the Print dialog) shows exactly how the printed pages will look.

questions.q: What does the magnifying-glass tool do in Print Preview?
o: Opens the Page Setup dialog box
Zooms in and out on the previewed page
questions.e: Clicking with the magnifying-glass pointer (or using the Zoom button) toggles between zoomed-in and full-page views for checking detail.

questions.q: How do you move to the next page while viewing a multi-page document in Print Preview?
o: Close the preview and reopen it
questions.e: Print Preview includes Next Page and Previous Page buttons for stepping through a multi-page printout.

questions.q: How do you return to the normal worksheet view from Print Preview without printing?
questions.e: Pressing Esc or clicking Close exits Print Preview and returns to the regular worksheet without sending anything to the printer.

questions.q: Can you send a document to the printer directly from the Print Preview screen?
o: Only if Draft Quality is off
No, you must close preview first
Yes, using the Print button available in the preview screen
questions.e: Print Preview includes its own Print button, letting you print immediately once the layout looks correct.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of checking Print Preview before printing?
o: To change the file's data values
To see the exact final layout — margins, headers, breaks — without using paper
questions.e: Print Preview shows the true final appearance of each printed page, catching layout problems before wasting paper and ink.

questions.q: What is a workbook in Excel?
o: The Excel file itself, which can contain worksheets, chart sheets and macro sheets
A printed report generated from a worksheet
A single row of data within a worksheet
A type of chart embedded in a worksheet
questions.e: A workbook is the Excel file — the container that can hold worksheets, chart sheets and macro sheets.

questions.q: How many worksheets does the default new workbook ('Book1') open with?
questions.e: A new default workbook opens with 3 worksheets, though this number can be changed in Excel Options.

questions.q: Can the default number of worksheets in a new workbook be changed?
questions.e: The default sheet count for new workbooks can be changed in Excel Options.

questions.q: Besides worksheets, what other sheet types can a workbook contain?
questions.e: A workbook can contain worksheets, chart sheets, and macro sheets.

questions.q: What is a chart sheet?
o: A sheet made up entirely of a single chart, on its own tab
A sheet that stores only macros
A worksheet that contains no data at all
A worksheet that has been hidden from view
questions.e: A chart sheet is a sheet dedicated to a single chart, on its own tab.

questions.q: Which keyboard shortcut opens the Open dialog box in Excel?
questions.e: Ctrl+O opens the Open dialog box so you can browse for and open an existing workbook.

questions.q: Which menu path opens an existing workbook from Backstage view?
questions.e: File > Open takes you to the Backstage view where you can browse to open a workbook.

questions.q: What does clicking 'Browse' inside the Open screen let you do?
o: Protect the workbook with a password
Navigate through drives and folders to locate a file
questions.e: Browse opens the standard file-browser dialog so you can navigate to the workbook's folder.

questions.q: To select several ADJACENT file names in the Open dialog, which technique do you use?
questions.e: Shift+click selects the first and last file clicked, plus every file listed in between — ideal for adjacent names.

questions.q: To select several NON-ADJACENT file names in the Open dialog, which technique do you use?
questions.e: Ctrl+click lets you pick individual files one at a time, regardless of where they sit in the list.

questions.q: What are the two types of password protection an Excel workbook can have?
o: Password to Open and Password to Modify
questions.e: Excel workbooks can be protected with a Password to Open (required to view the file) and/or a Password to Modify (required to save changes).

questions.q: A workbook has a 'Password to Modify' but no 'Password to Open'. What happens when you open it without the password?
o: The file refuses to open at all without it
It opens fully editable regardless of the password
It deletes itself from the folder
It opens, but you cannot save changes under the same name without the password
questions.e: A Password to Modify lets the file open, but saving changes back requires the correct password.

questions.q: Why might a workbook fail to open even though you typed the correct password letters?
o: Passwords are case-sensitive, so the capitalization must match exactly
questions.e: Excel passwords are case-sensitive — 'Report24' and 'report24' are treated as different passwords.

questions.q: Which of these file types can Excel import directly through File > Open?
o: Text files, Lotus 1-2-3, Quattro Pro, Works 2.0, dBASE and HTML documents, among others
Only image files such as JPEG
questions.e: Excel supports importing many foreign formats, including Text, Lotus 1-2-3, Quattro Pro, Works 2.0, dBASE, Excel 4 files and HTML documents.

questions.q: Can Excel open HTML documents and pull their table data into a worksheet?
o: Yes, HTML documents are among the importable file types
questions.e: HTML documents are one of the file types Excel can import, converting web-page tables into worksheet data.

questions.q: What file extension is used for the standard modern Excel workbook?
questions.e: The Excel workbook file type uses the extension .xls (older) or .xlsx (modern).

questions.q: What file extension identifies a legacy Excel chart saved as its own file?
questions.e: The .xlc extension identifies a standalone Excel chart file.

questions.q: What file extension identifies a legacy Excel macro sheet?
questions.e: The .xlm extension identifies an Excel macro sheet, used for older Excel 4.0-style macros.

questions.q: What extension pattern is used for Lotus 1-2-3 worksheet files?
questions.e: Lotus 1-2-3 files use extensions like .wk1, .wk3 and .wk4 — generally written as .wk*.

questions.q: Which file type below is a plain, tab- or comma-separated data file?
questions.e: Text files (.txt) hold plain data separated by tabs or commas, importable via the Text Import Wizard.

questions.q: How often is it recommended you save your workbook while working?
o: Only when you finish for the day
questions.e: Saving every 10–15 minutes limits how much unsaved work would be lost to a crash or power failure.

questions.q: What is the key difference between Save and Save As?
o: Save As only works for PDFs
Save overwrites the same file; Save As creates a new copy under a chosen name/location/type
Save creates a copy while Save As overwrites the original
questions.e: Save updates the existing file in place; Save As lets you save a new copy with a different name, location, or file type.

questions.q: Which command should you use to save a brand-new workbook for the very first time?
questions.e: Since a new workbook has no name or location yet, Save As (or the F12 shortcut) is required the first time.

questions.q: Which keyboard shortcut opens the Save As dialog?
questions.e: F12 is the keyboard shortcut for Save As, prompting for a file name and location.

questions.q: After a workbook has already been saved once, which method updates it without opening any dialog?
questions.e: Ctrl+S (or File > Save, or the Quick Access Save icon) silently overwrites the already-named, already-located file.

questions.q: Besides Ctrl+S and File > Save, what other control saves an already-saved file?
o: The Print button on the ribbon
The Save icon on the Quick Access toolbar
The Undo button on the toolbar
The Redo button on the toolbar
questions.e: Clicking the Save icon on the Quick Access toolbar saves the file the same way Ctrl+S does.

questions.q: What must you complete in the Save As dialog when saving for the first time?
o: A file name and a destination folder
questions.e: The Save As dialog requires you to specify the file name and where (which folder/path) it will be saved.

questions.q: On Windows 7–10, what is the maximum length of a file name, including spaces?
questions.e: Windows 7 through 10 allow file names up to 255 characters long, including spaces.

questions.q: Which of the following characters is FORBIDDEN in a Windows file name?
questions.e: The forward slash (/) is one of the forbidden characters, along with ? : * ' !

questions.q: Which of the following characters is FORBIDDEN in a Windows file name?
questions.e: The asterisk (*) is forbidden in Windows file names, along with / ? : ' !

questions.q: Which of the following characters is FORBIDDEN in a Windows file name?
questions.e: The less-than sign ( !

questions.q: Is the old DOS '8.3 naming' rule (8-character name plus 3-character extension) still required for saving files in modern Excel?
o: Yes, it is still strictly enforced
No, file names are unlimited on all systems
Yes, but only for XLSX files
No, it is no longer required, though names may be truncated if moved to an older system
questions.e: 8.3 naming is no longer required, but a long name will be automatically truncated if transferred to a system that still enforces the old rule.

questions.q: Why should you avoid relying on a very long, descriptive file name if the file might be moved to an older system?
o: Older systems may enforce 8.3 naming and truncate the name automatically
Long names use more storage space
