Excel will refuse to open long file names
questions.e: Systems still enforcing legacy 8.3 naming will truncate a long file name when the file is transferred there.

questions.q: Which character below is allowed in a Windows file name?
questions.e: Spaces are explicitly allowed (up to the 255-character limit); ? ' and : are all forbidden.

questions.q: Where in Excel do you find the Protect Workbook options?
questions.e: File > Info reveals the Protect Workbook menu with several protection options.

questions.q: Which Protect Workbook option asks that anyone opening the file open it as read-only, without hard-blocking edits?
questions.e: Always Open Read-Only is a soft suggestion to open the file read-only, discouraging (not strictly preventing) accidental edits.

questions.q: Which Protect Workbook option requires a password before the workbook can even be opened?
questions.e: Encrypt with Password sets a password required just to open the file at all.

questions.q: Which Protect Workbook option prevents worksheets from being added, deleted, moved, hidden or renamed?
questions.e: Protect Workbook Structure locks the arrangement of sheets themselves, not the cell contents.

questions.q: Which Protect Workbook option restricts editing within the active worksheet, such as locking specific cells?
questions.e: Protect Current Sheet restricts changes to the active worksheet, e.g. locking cells from editing.

questions.q: Which Protect Workbook option applies Information Rights Management (IRM) so only authorized people can open, edit, print, or forward the file?
questions.e: Restrict Access applies IRM permissions controlling exactly who can open, edit, print or forward the workbook.

questions.q: When you set a new password on a workbook, what does Excel always require you to do?
o: Type the password a second time to confirm it
Print a backup copy of the file first
questions.e: Excel requires confirming the password by typing it again, to guard against a typo locking you out.

questions.q: Which keyboard shortcut closes the active workbook?
questions.e: Ctrl+F4 closes the currently active workbook.

questions.q: Besides Ctrl+F4, what other actions close a workbook?
o: Pressing Ctrl+Z twice in a row
File > Close, or the title bar close button
Right-clicking a cell and choosing Format
questions.e: File > Close and the title bar's × button both close the current workbook.

questions.q: What happens if you try to close a workbook that has unsaved changes?
o: Excel crashes and loses all data
Excel closes without warning and loses the data
Excel prompts you to Save, Don't Save, or Cancel
questions.e: Excel prompts with Save, Don't Save, and Cancel options so you don't lose unsaved edits by accident.

questions.q: In the Open dialog box, how do you copy or move a file to a different folder?
o: Right-click the file, choose Copy or Cut, navigate to the destination, then Paste
Drag the Excel window title bar around
Double-click the file twice quickly to open it
Press Ctrl+P to open the print dialog
questions.e: Right-click gives Copy/Cut options; after navigating to the destination folder, Paste completes the copy or move.

questions.q: In the Open dialog box, how do you delete a file?
o: Right-click it and choose Delete, then confirm
Drag it into a new workbook
questions.e: Right-clicking a file in the Open dialog and choosing Delete removes it (after a confirmation prompt).

questions.q: What is the quickest way to insert a single new worksheet at the end of the tab list?
o: Press Ctrl+N to open a new workbook
Press Ctrl+F4 to close the window
Click the ⊕ button at the bottom, next to the last sheet tab
Right-click any cell and choose Insert Sheet
questions.e: The quick-insert (+) button at the bottom of the screen adds a new blank sheet instantly.

questions.q: Which ribbon path inserts a new worksheet before the active tab?
questions.e: Home > Cells > Insert > Insert Sheet adds a new worksheet before the currently active tab.

questions.q: How can you insert several new worksheets at once?
o: Shift-select the same number of existing tabs, then use Insert Sheet
It cannot be done in a single action
Copy the workbook and merge it back in
questions.e: Selecting multiple existing tabs with Shift before choosing Insert Sheet adds that many new sheets in one step.

questions.q: What are the two ways to rename a worksheet tab?
o: Right-click the tab and choose Rename, or double-click the tab name
Only through the File > Info screen
Press Ctrl+R to rename the tab
questions.e: You can right-click a tab and choose Rename, or simply double-click directly on the tab's name.

questions.q: Which ribbon path deletes the active worksheet?
questions.e: Home > Cells > Delete > Delete Sheet removes the currently selected worksheet.

questions.q: Besides the ribbon, how else can you delete a worksheet?
o: Press the spacebar to select it
Right-click the sheet's tab and choose Delete
questions.e: Right-clicking a sheet tab and choosing Delete from the shortcut menu also removes the sheet.

questions.q: Which menu command opens the Consolidate dialog box?
questions.e: Data > Consolidate opens the dialog used to combine data from multiple ranges.

questions.q: What must you select BEFORE opening the Consolidate dialog?
o: The destination range where the summary will appear
Nothing needs to be selected first
The print area of the worksheet
questions.e: You first select the destination range — where the combined, consolidated result should be placed.

questions.q: In the Consolidate dialog, what does the Function dropdown let you choose?
o: The file format to save as
The chart type used for the summary
A summary function such as Sum, Average, or Count to apply across the sources
The worksheet color used for tabs
questions.e: The Function dropdown selects how the source values are combined, e.g. Sum, Average, Count, Max or Min.

questions.q: What do the Top Row and Left Column checkboxes control in the Consolidate dialog?
o: Whether to print row and column headings
Whether to consolidate by matching headings instead of by plain cell position
questions.e: Checking Top Row and/or Left Column tells Excel to match source data by its heading labels rather than by raw cell position.

questions.q: Consolidating 'by position' requires what about the source worksheets?
o: They must be laid out identically, with data in the same row/column order on every sheet
They must all be password protected
They must all be chart sheets
questions.e: Position-based consolidation assumes every source sheet has matching data in the exact same cells, so the layouts must be identical.

questions.q: If the source worksheets list the same categories but in a different order on each sheet, which consolidation approach should you use?
o: By position, matching cell locations exactly
By category, using Top Row / Left Column matching
Neither works; you must retype the data
Only the Sum function can be used
questions.e: When category order differs between sheets, consolidating by heading (Top Row/Left Column) matches values correctly regardless of position.

questions.q: What is the effect of checking 'Create links to source data' in the Consolidate dialog?
o: The consolidated values become fixed and never change
The consolidated values update automatically whenever the source data changes
It converts the summary into a chart
questions.e: Checking the links option inserts formulas that reference the sources, so the summary refreshes automatically as source data changes.

questions.q: If you leave 'Create links to source data' unchecked, what kind of values are placed in the destination range?
o: Chart images pasted into the range
Fixed values that will not update if the sources change later
questions.e: Without links, Consolidate inserts a one-time snapshot of fixed values rather than live formulas.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of a chart in Excel?
o: To give a visual summary of patterns and trends in data
To store raw numbers more compactly than a table
questions.e: A chart's main job is to make patterns, trends and comparisons in data easier to see at a glance than scanning raw numbers.

questions.q: Which tab do you use to insert a chart manually?
questions.e: Charts are inserted from the Insert tab on the ribbon, after selecting the data to plot.

questions.q: Where can an embedded chart be placed?
o: In the same worksheet as its data
questions.e: An embedded chart sits directly on the worksheet that holds its source data, as opposed to a chart placed on its own chart sheet.

questions.q: What happens to a chart when its linked source data changes?
o: Nothing, until the file is reopened
The chart must be deleted and rebuilt
questions.e: A chart is linked to its source cells via a series formula, so editing the underlying values redraws the chart automatically.

questions.q: What is a Data Series?
o: A set of related data points, usually from one row or column
The title displayed above a chart
questions.e: A data series groups related values — typically all the entries in one row or one column — that are plotted together in a chart.

questions.q: What is a Data Point?
o: A single value from a data series represented by one bar/slice/marker
The gap between two axis tick marks
questions.e: A data point is one individual value within a series, shown on the chart as one bar, one pie slice, or one marker.

questions.q: What does the Legend show?
o: Which color/pattern corresponds to each data series
The formula used to calculate totals
questions.e: The legend is the key that tells you which color, pattern or marker on the chart belongs to which data series.

questions.q: What is a Marker?
o: The symbol marking an individual data point on a line/scatter chart
questions.e: Markers are the small symbols (dots, squares, triangles) used to highlight individual data points, especially on line and scatter charts.

questions.q: What is the Plot Area?
o: The region bounded by the axes where the data series are drawn
The area where formulas are typed
The border around the entire worksheet
The space reserved for the chart title only
questions.e: The plot area is the rectangular space inside the axes where the actual bars, lines or slices of the chart appear.

questions.q: What is a Tick mark?
o: A small line dividing an axis into equal segments
A symbol showing a formula error
A shortcut key for bold text
questions.e: Tick marks are the small lines crossing an axis at regular intervals, lining up with axis labels or gridlines.

questions.q: Which chart type is best for showing each category's share of a single total?
questions.e: A Pie chart plots one data series and shows how each category contributes to that one overall total.

questions.q: Which subtype lets you show more than one data series as concentric rings, similar to a pie chart?
questions.e: A Doughnut chart works like a Pie chart but can display multiple data series, each drawn as its own ring.

questions.q: Which chart type is best for showing a trend over time at even intervals?
questions.e: Line charts connect evenly spaced data points, making them ideal for showing how a value trends over time.

questions.q: Which chart type uses vertical bars to compare values across categories?
questions.e: A Column chart compares values across categories using vertical bars; stacked subtypes also show how parts make up a whole.

questions.q: Which chart type is the horizontal equivalent of a Column chart, useful for long category names?
questions.e: A Bar chart makes the same category comparisons as a Column chart but runs horizontally, which suits long category labels.

questions.q: Which chart type should you use when x-axis spacing is uneven or you are comparing many/large datasets of numeric pairs?
questions.e: XY (Scatter) charts plot pairs of numeric values and are the right choice when category spacing is uneven or datasets are large.

questions.q: Which chart type emphasizes the magnitude of change over time by filling the area beneath the line?
questions.e: Area charts fill the space under the plotted line, drawing attention to the size of the change over time.

questions.q: Which chart type compares several data series across multiple variables radiating from a central point?
questions.e: Radar charts plot each variable on its own axis radiating from a center point, useful for comparing multiple series across several dimensions.

questions.q: Which chart type shows trends across two dimensions using color bands/contours over a 3-D surface?
questions.e: Surface charts use color bands or contour lines over a 3-D surface to show how values trend across two dimensions at once.

questions.q: Which chart type compares three sets of values, with a third variable shown as marker size?
questions.e: Bubble charts plot two values as x/y position and a third value as the size of the bubble marker.

questions.q: Which chart type illustrates fluctuating values such as share prices over time (e.g. High-Low-Close)?
questions.e: Stock charts (High-Low-Close, Open-High-Low-Close, etc.) are designed to illustrate fluctuating values such as stock prices.

questions.q: Which Column chart subtype shows each category's total as 100%, with segments proportional within it?
questions.e: 100% Stacked Column normalizes every category to a full 100% bar, showing each series' proportional share within it.

questions.q: How do you emphasize one slice of a pie chart by pulling it out from the rest?
o: Change the chart type to Bar
Add a legend to the chart
Explode the slice out from the pie
questions.e: Exploding a pie slice — dragging it outward from the rest of the pie — visually separates and emphasizes that one category.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the 14 standard Excel chart types covered in this module?
questions.e: Column, Bar, Line, Pie, Doughnut, Area, XY (Scatter), Radar, Surface, Bubble and Stock make up the standard chart types covered here — Histogram is not among them.

questions.q: What is the first step when creating a chart manually via the Insert tab?
questions.e: You must first select the data range you want charted, including headers, so Excel can build correct axis labels and a legend.

questions.q: After selecting a chart type and format, what button is used to add titles and axis labels?
questions.e: The Layout button/tab that appears with a selected chart is where you add chart titles, axis titles, data labels and legend placement.

questions.q: What keyboard shortcut instantly creates a default chart on a new chart sheet?
questions.e: Pressing F11 with data selected instantly builds a default chart on its own new chart sheet.

questions.q: What keyboard shortcut instantly creates an embedded default chart on the current worksheet?
questions.e: Alt+F1 creates the same default chart as F11, but embeds it directly on the current worksheet instead of a new chart sheet.

questions.q: What is Excel's default chart type when using F11 or Alt+F1?
questions.e: Both automatic-chart shortcuts fall back to Excel's default chart type, the 2-D Clustered Column chart.

questions.q: When Excel auto-creates a chart from a selection, along which side does it place the category axis?
o: The longer side of the selected range
There is no rule — it is random
questions.e: Excel's convention is to run the category (x) axis along whichever side of the selection — rows or columns — is longer.

questions.q: In automatic chart creation, what do the labels from the shorter side of the selection usually become?
questions.e: The shorter side's labels typically end up as the legend entries or series/chart titles rather than plotted category values.

questions.q: What can happen if a 'category' column selected for a chart actually contains only numbers?
o: Excel refuses to build the chart
The chart is created without any axis
Excel may treat it as a data series and auto-number the categories instead
questions.e: All-numeric cells in what should be the category range can be misread as a data series, with Excel auto-numbering categories 1, 2, 3, … instead.

questions.q: Why should you include header text when selecting data for a chart?
o: So Excel reads it as labels instead of numeric data
questions.e: Text headers are needed so Excel reads them as labels for axes and the legend, rather than treating the header row as part of the plotted numeric data.

questions.q: Which button in the ribbon lets you walk step-by-step through chart type, data range, and title choices?
questions.e: The Chart Wizard button guides you step-by-step through picking a chart type, confirming the data range, and adding titles/labels.

questions.q: What keeps a chart linked to its underlying worksheet cells?
questions.e: A chart's series formula (visible in the formula bar when a series is selected) defines exactly which cells feed the chart, keeping it linked.

questions.q: If rows are inserted or deleted so a chart's data range grows or shrinks, what may be needed?
o: Manually redefining the chart's data range
questions.e: Automatic updating tracks the original linked range, so when that range changes shape, the chart's series/data range may need to be redefined manually.

questions.q: Does a chart saved/pasted as a static image continue to update automatically?
o: No — a static image is no longer linked to the data
Yes, images update exactly like embedded charts
Only if the workbook stays open
Only on chart sheets, not embedded charts
questions.e: Once a chart is saved or pasted as a picture, it loses its link to the worksheet cells and will not reflect later data changes.

questions.q: How is an embedded chart saved?
o: It must be exported separately as an image first
Only if 'Save Chart' is chosen from a special menu
It cannot be saved, only printed
questions.e: An embedded chart is just an object on the worksheet, so it is saved automatically whenever the workbook itself is saved.

questions.q: Where do you go to print a chart?
questions.e: Printing a chart starts from File > Print Preview, where the Setup button opens further page and margin options.

questions.q: In Print Preview, which option scales a chart to fill the entire printed page?
questions.e: On the Margins tab of the Setup dialog, the 'Use Full Page' option scales the chart so it fills the whole printed page.

questions.q: What does sorting data mean?
o: Arranging data into ascending or descending order
Hiding rows that don't meet a condition
questions.e: Sorting rearranges records into ascending (A–Z, smallest–largest) or descending (Z–A, largest–smallest) order.

questions.q: In a data table used for sorting, what does a row represent?
questions.e: Each row of a data table is treated as one record — sorting moves whole records together, keeping their fields aligned.

questions.q: In a data table used for sorting, what does a column represent?
questions.e: Each column represents one field — a single piece of information (e.g. a mark) repeated across every record.

questions.q: Which ribbon buttons perform a quick single-column ascending sort?
o: Home > Sort & Filter > Sort A to Z
questions.e: Home > Sort & Filter > Sort A to Z performs a quick ascending sort based on the selected column.

questions.q: Which button performs a quick single-column descending sort?
questions.e: Sort Z to A, next to Sort A to Z under Sort & Filter, arranges the selected column in descending order.

questions.q: If you need to sort by a column other than the first column, what should you use?
questions.e: Custom Sort opens the Sort dialog box, letting you explicitly pick any column to sort by, not just the first one.

questions.q: In the Sort dialog box, what two things do you choose for a sort level?
o: The column to sort by, and the sort order
questions.e: Each level of the Sort dialog requires choosing which column (field) to sort by and whether the order is ascending or descending.

questions.q: What button adds a secondary 'Then By' rule for a multi-column sort?
questions.e: Clicking 'Add Level' in the Sort dialog adds a new 'Then By' row used to break ties left by the level above it.

questions.q: A class is sorted ascending by CSM 201; two students tie. Which setting breaks the tie using CSM 203, highest first?
o: Add a 'Then By' level: CSM 203, Descending
Add a 'Then By' level: CSM 203, Ascending
Sort by CSM 203 only, ignoring CSM 201
Use Sort A to Z on the Name column
questions.e: A 'Then By' level sorting CSM 203 in descending order breaks ties left after the primary ascending CSM 201 sort, ranking tied students by highest CSM 203 first.

questions.q: In a multi-column sort with CSM 201 ascending then CSM 203 descending as tiebreaker, which column is the primary sort key?
questions.e: The first level set in the Sort dialog — CSM 201 — is the primary sort key; CSM 203 only applies to break ties within it.

questions.q: What does filtering data do?
o: Deletes rows that don't match criteria
Displays only the rows that meet specified criteria, hiding the rest
Converts filtered rows into a chart
questions.e: Filtering temporarily hides rows that don't match a condition while keeping the matching rows visible — nothing is deleted.

questions.q: Does filtering delete the hidden rows?
o: No — hidden rows are still present, just not displayed
Only rows with errors are deleted
questions.e: Filtered-out rows remain in the worksheet; they are simply hidden from view until the filter is removed.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a way Excel lets you filter a single column?
o: By list values in a column
By color and list value combined at once
questions.e: Excel allows filtering by list values, by format, or by criteria on a column — but not two of these methods combined at the same time.

questions.q: What are the three ways you can filter data in Excel?
o: By formula, by macro, by chart
By list values, by format, or by criteria
By worksheet, by workbook, by add-in
By font, by border, by comment
questions.e: AutoFilter supports filtering by ticking list values, by cell format (color/icon), or by a logical/numeric criterion.

questions.q: What is the first step to turn on AutoFilter for a table?
questions.e: AutoFilter needs the header row selected so Excel knows where the field names are and can attach dropdown arrows there.

questions.q: After selecting the header row, which ribbon command turns filtering on?
questions.e: Home > Sort & Filter > Filter switches on the dropdown arrows for AutoFilter across the header row.

questions.q: Once Filter is turned on, where do you click to set a condition for one column?
o: The dropdown arrow on that column's header
The worksheet tab at the bottom
The Name Box beside the formula bar
The status bar at the bottom
questions.e: Each header cell gets a dropdown arrow; clicking it opens the list of values and the Number/Text/Date Filter options for that column.

questions.q: To find students who failed CSM 203 (mark below 40), which Number Filter condition do you choose?
questions.e: 'Less Than' with a threshold of 40 shows only rows where the CSM 203 mark is below the pass mark.

questions.q: In the worked example, what threshold value is entered to filter out students who passed CSM 203?
questions.e: The pass mark used in the worked example is 40, so 'Less Than 40' isolates the students who failed.

questions.q: Which Number Filter condition would you use to find students who scored above 70?
questions.e: 'Greater Than' with a threshold of 70 shows only rows where the mark exceeds 70.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of Microsoft PowerPoint?
questions.e: PowerPoint is presentation software used to transform ideas into professional slideshows, such as sales reports or personal presentations.

questions.q: What is the correct way to start PowerPoint from the Start button?
o: Right-click the desktop and choose PowerPoint
Click Start, search "PowerPoint", click the icon
Open File Explorer and search for .pptx files
Open any Office app and switch to PowerPoint
questions.e: You click the Start button, type "PowerPoint" into the search box, and click the PowerPoint icon in the results.

questions.q: In Backstage View, what are the two main ways to start a new presentation?
o: Recover from Recycle Bin or cloud backup
Open a PDF or a video file
questions.e: Backstage View (File > New) offers a Blank Presentation with no design elements, or a template with a pre-set colour scheme and layout.

questions.q: When creating a presentation from a template, what is the typical sequence of steps?
o: Click Create, then pick a template afterwards
Type text first, then apply a template
Save the file, then select a template
Choose a template, choose a colour scheme, click Create
questions.e: You choose a template, optionally choose a colour scheme variant, then click Create to generate the new presentation.

questions.q: What layout does a brand-new PowerPoint presentation's first slide use by default?
questions.e: A new presentation always opens with one slide using the Title Slide layout, with placeholders for a title and a subtitle.

questions.q: Which Backstage View option starts a presentation with no colour scheme or design elements applied?
questions.e: Blank Presentation opens with the plain default Office Theme and no pre-set design elements, giving full creative control.

questions.q: What does choosing a template in Backstage View give you, compared to Blank Presentation?
o: A pre-designed colour scheme and layout
questions.e: A template comes with a pre-designed colour scheme and layout already applied, unlike the plain Blank Presentation option.

questions.q: Which menu do you open to reach Backstage View and create a new presentation?
questions.e: Clicking File opens Backstage View, which includes the New command for creating a new presentation.

questions.q: What is a placeholder on a PowerPoint slide?
o: A dotted-border area reserved for text, pictures, charts, etc.
A backup copy of the presentation
A hidden slide that isn't shown in the show
questions.e: A placeholder is a dotted-border container on a slide meant to hold a specific type of content, such as text, a picture, a chart or SmartArt.

questions.q: Which icons commonly appear inside an empty content placeholder?
o: Insert Picture, Insert Chart, Insert SmartArt
questions.e: An empty content placeholder shows small icons for quickly inserting a Picture, a Chart, or a SmartArt Graphic directly into that placeholder.

questions.q: What does a slide's "layout" refer to?
o: The file format used to save the slide
The order of slides in the presentation
The arrangement of placeholders on the slide
The colour theme applied to the slide
questions.e: A slide layout is the arrangement of placeholders on a slide — for example, "Title and Content" — and each layout has a descriptive name.

questions.q: How do you insert text into a placeholder?
o: Drag a text file onto the slide
Right-click and choose Paste Special only
Double-click the slide thumbnail in the Slides tab
Click inside it, type, then click outside to finish
questions.e: You click inside the placeholder to activate it, type your text, then click outside the placeholder to finish editing.

questions.q: Where do you go to insert a brand-new slide with a chosen layout?
questions.e: New slides are inserted from the Home tab's New Slide command, which also lets you pick a specific layout from its drop-down.

questions.q: How do you change the layout of a slide that already has content?
o: Home tab > Layout, then choose a different layout
Delete the slide and start over
questions.e: Selecting the slide and using Home tab > Layout lets you switch to a different arrangement of placeholders without deleting the slide.

questions.q: How do you reorder slides by moving one to a new position?
o: Apply a new theme to the slide
Drag its thumbnail to a new spot in the Slides tab
questions.e: Clicking and dragging a slide's thumbnail within the Slides tab repositions it in the presentation.

questions.q: Which PowerPoint view is the default view used for adding and editing content on individual slides?
questions.e: Normal view is the default editing view, showing the Slides tab, the current slide, and often a notes pane.

questions.q: Which view shows thumbnails of every slide in a grid, ideal for reordering slides?
questions.e: Slide Sorter view displays all slides as thumbnails in a grid, making it easy to see the whole flow and drag slides into a new order.

questions.q: Which view plays the presentation full-screen exactly as an audience would see it?
questions.e: Slide Show view runs the presentation full-screen, one slide at a time, as it would appear to a live audience.

questions.q: When should you use Save As instead of Save?
o: The first time you save a presentation, or to save a copy
Every time you make a small change
questions.e: Save As is used the first time a file is saved (or to save a new copy), letting you choose the location, file type and filename.

questions.q: What does the Save command do after a presentation has already been saved once?
o: Creates a brand-new copy each time
Converts the file to PDF automatically
Opens the Save As dialog again
Updates the existing file in place with no dialog box
questions.e: After the first save, using Save simply updates the same file with your latest changes, without prompting for a name or location.

questions.q: Which file extension is the default format for a PowerPoint 2013/2016 presentation?
questions.e: .pptx is the default PowerPoint Presentation format used by PowerPoint 2013/2016.

questions.q: Which file extension indicates a macro-enabled PowerPoint presentation?
questions.e: .pptm is the Macro-Enabled Presentation format, used when the file contains macros.

questions.q: Which file extension is used to save a presentation compatible with PowerPoint 97-2003?
questions.e: .ppt is the PowerPoint 97-2003 Presentation format, kept for compatibility with older versions of PowerPoint.

questions.q: Which file format saves the presentation as a fixed, non-editable document rather than an editable slide file?
questions.e: .pdf (Portable Document Format) saves the presentation as a PDF document instead of an editable PowerPoint file.

questions.q: Which file extension opens directly in Slide Show view instead of Normal view when double-clicked?
questions.e: .pps/.ppsx (PowerPoint Show) launches straight into full-screen Slide Show view rather than the editing view.

questions.q: You want recipients to double-click a file and have it launch straight into a full-screen show. Which format should you choose?
questions.e: .ppsx (PowerPoint Show) is designed to open directly in Slide Show view, skipping Normal editing view entirely.

questions.q: How do you delete text located to the left of the cursor?
questions.e: Backspace removes text to the left of the text cursor, while Delete removes text to the right.

questions.q: What appears near selected text to offer quick formatting commands?
questions.e: Selecting text triggers a small hover toolbar with commonly used formatting commands like Bold, Italic and font choices.

questions.q: What benefit does the Font Size drop-down provide as you hover over each size option?
o: A live preview of that size applied to the selected text
questions.e: Hovering over a font size in the drop-down shows a live preview on the selected text before you click to apply it.

questions.q: Which command lets you pick a text colour beyond the standard palette shown in the drop-down?
questions.e: The Font Color drop-down includes a "More Colors" option for choosing custom colours outside the standard palette.

questions.q: Which three basic emphasis commands are commonly grouped together on the Home tab?
questions.e: Bold, Italic and Underline are the standard text-emphasis commands available on the Home tab.

questions.q: Which commands let you nudge selected text's size up or down without opening the size drop-down list?
questions.e: Increase Font Size and Decrease Font Size step the text size up or down one increment at a time.

questions.q: Which command removes all formatting from selected text, returning it to the default style?
questions.e: Clear All Formatting strips bold, italics, colour and other formatting, restoring the plain default text style.

questions.q: Which command adds a drop shadow effect behind selected text?
questions.e: Text Shadow adds a shadow effect behind the selected text for emphasis.

questions.q: Do the Align Left, Center, Align Right and Justify commands align text relative to the whole slide or to the placeholder?
o: Relative to its own placeholder or text box
questions.e: These alignment commands position text within its own placeholder or text box, not relative to other objects on the slide.

questions.q: Which alignment option stretches each line (except the last) to fill the full width of the placeholder?
questions.e: Justify stretches every line except the last one so text fills the entire width of the placeholder or text box.

questions.q: What is a PowerPoint theme?
o: A predefined combination of colours, fonts and effects
A saved list of quiz questions
questions.e: A theme is a predefined set of colours, fonts and visual effects applied consistently across a presentation.

questions.q: What is the name of PowerPoint's default theme in a new blank presentation?
questions.e: The Office Theme is the default theme applied automatically to a new blank presentation.

questions.q: Where do you go to apply a different theme to a presentation?
questions.e: Themes are browsed and applied from the Design tab's Themes group.

questions.q: What happens when you hover over a theme thumbnail in the Themes group before clicking it?
o: It opens the Insert Table dialog
A live preview shows on the current slide
questions.e: Hovering over a theme thumbnail shows a live preview of that theme applied to the current slide, without committing to it.

questions.q: What is one advantage of applying a theme before adding slide content?
o: You can use live preview to see exactly how your finished content will look as you choose
It converts the file to PDF
It prevents you from changing the theme later
questions.e: Applying a theme before typing content lets you preview how the theme will render with your actual text, sizes and colours as you choose it.

questions.q: What is created when you customise a theme's colours, fonts or effects and save the result?
questions.e: Modifying a theme's colours, fonts or effects and saving it produces a new custom theme that can be reused later.

questions.q: What are Background Styles based on?
o: The number of slides in the deck
questions.e: Background Styles are fill variations generated from the colours of the currently applied theme.

questions.q: What happens to applied background styles when the presentation's theme is changed?
o: They convert to a picture background
They are deleted and must be reapplied manually
They stay exactly the same regardless of the theme
They update automatically to match the new theme's colours
questions.e: Because background styles are built from theme colours, they update automatically whenever a different theme is applied.

questions.q: How do you insert a new, free-standing text box onto a slide?
o: Insert tab > Text Box, then drag on the slide
questions.e: Insert tab > Text Box activates drawing mode; you then click and drag on the slide to create the text box.

questions.q: How do you move a selected text box to a new position on the slide?
o: Click its border and drag it
questions.e: Clicking the border of a selected text box and dragging moves it to a new location on the slide.

questions.q: What do you drag to resize a selected text box?
questions.e: Small sizing handles appear around a selected object's edges and corners; dragging one resizes the box.

questions.q: What is the key difference between copy/paste and drag-and-drop when moving text?
o: They are identical in every way
Copy/paste duplicates the text; drag-and-drop moves it
questions.e: Copy/paste leaves the original text in place and adds a duplicate elsewhere, while drag-and-drop relocates the text without duplicating it.

questions.q: What key do you press to start a new bullet or numbered line while typing in a content placeholder?
questions.e: Pressing Enter after a list item starts a new bulleted or numbered line at the same level.

questions.q: How do you set a picture as the bullet symbol for a list?
o: Bullets drop-down > Bullets and Numbering > Picture
questions.e: In the Bullets and Numbering dialog, the Picture button lets you choose an image file to use as the bullet symbol.

questions.q: How do you use a special character (e.g. from Wingdings) as a bullet?
o: Bullets drop-down > Customize > Symbol dialog, choose a Font
questions.e: Bullets and Numbering > Customize opens the Symbol dialog, where the Font drop-down (such as Wingdings) lets you pick a symbol character as the bullet.

questions.q: How do you change a numbered list to start counting from a number other than 1?
o: Use the Start at: field in Bullets and Numbering
questions.e: The Numbering drop-down's Bullets and Numbering dialog includes a Start at: field to set the list's first number.

questions.q: How do you remove bullets from a list, leaving plain paragraph text?
o: Click the Bullets command again to toggle it off
Apply a new theme to the slide
questions.e: Clicking the active Bullets (or Numbering) command a second time toggles the list formatting off, leaving plain text.

questions.q: Which dialog box appears when you insert a table using a content placeholder's Insert Table icon?
o: Insert Table dialog, asking for rows and columns
Format Background pane for the slide
questions.e: Clicking the Insert Table icon in a placeholder opens the Insert Table dialog, where you specify the number of columns and rows.

questions.q: How do you insert a table using the Ribbon instead of a placeholder icon?
o: Insert tab > Table, then drag across the grid
questions.e: Insert tab > Table opens a visual grid; dragging across it selects the number of rows and columns before you click to insert.

questions.q: Which key moves the cursor to the next cell in a table, wrapping to the start of the next row?
questions.e: Tab advances to the next cell in a table; in the last cell, pressing Tab adds a brand-new row.

questions.q: Besides the mouse and Tab key, what else can be used to move between table cells one at a time?
questions.e: Arrow keys move the cursor up, down, left or right one cell at a time within a table.

questions.q: Which contextual Ribbon tab contains the Rows & Columns group for editing a table's structure?
questions.e: Clicking inside a table activates the contextual Table Tools tabs; the Rows & Columns group is on the Layout tab.

questions.q: Which command in the Rows & Columns group adds a new row directly above the cursor's current row?
questions.e: Insert Above adds a new row immediately above the row containing the cursor.

questions.q: What is an alternate way to insert or delete rows/columns without using the Layout tab?
o: Press Ctrl+P to print the slide
Right-click inside a table cell for a context menu
questions.e: Right-clicking inside a table cell opens a context menu offering the same Insert and Delete row/column commands as the Layout tab.

questions.q: Why do presenters add pictures, clip art, video and sound to slides?
o: To communicate graphically, beyond what text alone can convey
To replace the need for a title slide
To disable the need for speaker notes
questions.e: Multimedia elements let a slide communicate visually and add impact beyond plain text.

questions.q: Which Ribbon tab and group contain the Insert Picture command?
questions.e: Insert Picture is found on the Insert tab, in the Illustrations group.

questions.q: Dragging a picture's corner sizing handle resizes it how?
o: Proportionally — height and width change together
questions.e: Corner handles keep the picture's original proportions while resizing.

questions.q: Dragging a picture's side (not corner) sizing handle usually results in what?
o: Distorted proportions, since only one dimension changes
questions.e: Side handles change only width or only height, stretching or squashing the image.

questions.q: How do you move a picture to a new position on the slide?
questions.e: Clicking on a selected picture and dragging repositions it on the slide.

questions.q: What does the green circle above a selected picture represent?
questions.e: The green circle is the Free Rotate handle; dragging it rotates the object freely.

questions.q: Which tab appears on the Ribbon when a picture is selected, offering styling tools?
questions.e: Selecting a picture displays the contextual Picture Tools Format tab.

questions.q: What does the More dropdown arrow in the Picture Styles gallery reveal?
o: A list of supported file formats
The undo history for the slide
A spell-check dialog for the text
The full set of Picture Styles, with live preview as you point to each
questions.e: Clicking More opens the complete gallery of ready-made picture styles, previewing each live on the slide.

questions.q: What does 'Change Picture Shape' do?
o: Crops the picture into a different outline shape, such as an oval or star
questions.e: Picture Shape reshapes the picture's outline/crop area into a chosen shape.

questions.q: Adding a Picture Border lets you set which two properties?
questions.e: A picture border has a chosen color and a chosen weight (thickness).

questions.q: Which Picture Tools Format feature trims unwanted edges from a picture?
questions.e: Cropping removes unwanted portions from the edges of a picture.

questions.q: Which Picture Tools Format feature reduces a picture's file size?
questions.e: Compressing pictures reduces file size, useful for keeping the presentation file smaller.

questions.q: Which command undoes all formatting changes applied to a picture, restoring its original appearance?
questions.e: Reset Picture removes all applied formatting and restores the original image.

questions.q: Adjusting Contrast on a picture changes what?
o: The file name of the picture
The difference between the light and dark areas of the image
questions.e: Contrast adjustment increases or decreases the tonal difference between light and dark regions.

questions.q: Which Picture Tools Format command applies a color tint or converts a picture to grayscale?
questions.e: Recolor changes the overall color treatment of a picture, e.g. grayscale or a color wash.

questions.q: Which Ribbon tab holds the SmartArt command?
questions.e: SmartArt is inserted from the Insert tab.

questions.q: After clicking SmartArt, what must you choose before clicking OK?
questions.e: The SmartArt gallery requires selecting a diagram type/layout before inserting it.

questions.q: An existing bulleted list on a slide can be turned into a SmartArt diagram by...
questions.e: PowerPoint can convert a bulleted list placeholder directly into a SmartArt graphic.

questions.q: Which SmartArt type is best suited to showing sequential steps in a task?
questions.e: A Process diagram represents an ordered sequence of steps.

questions.q: Which SmartArt type shows a continuous, repeating sequence of stages?
questions.e: A Cycle diagram illustrates a repeating, circular process.

questions.q: Which SmartArt type best represents an organization chart?
questions.e: Hierarchy diagrams show reporting/organizational structures, like an org chart.

questions.q: Which SmartArt type shows how parts relate to a whole, arranged in quadrants?
questions.e: Matrix diagrams display parts of a whole in quadrant form.

questions.q: Which SmartArt type builds proportional or hierarchical relationships from a base upward?
questions.e: Pyramid diagrams show foundational relationships building up from a base.

questions.q: Which SmartArt type is best for non-sequential, grouped blocks of information?
questions.e: List diagrams present grouped information without requiring a strict sequence.

questions.q: Which SmartArt type shows connections such as overlapping or converging ideas?
questions.e: Relationship diagrams depict connections between two or more ideas.

questions.q: How do you select multiple objects on a slide at once before aligning them?
o: Right-click each object individually and choose Copy
Click and drag a selection box around them
questions.e: Dragging a selection box (or Shift-clicking) around the objects selects them all.

questions.q: Which Ribbon tab contains the Align command?
questions.e: The Align command is on the (Drawing/Picture) Format tab.

questions.q: Align Center aligns selected objects along which line?
questions.e: Align Center lines objects up on a shared vertical center line (horizontal centering).

questions.q: Align Middle aligns selected objects along which line?
o: The bottom of the slide only
Along a 45° diagonal line across the slide
questions.e: Align Middle lines objects up on a shared horizontal center line (vertical centering).

questions.q: Align Top lines up the selected objects by their...
questions.e: Align Top lines the objects' top edges up along a common horizontal line.

questions.q: Align Left lines up the selected objects by their...
questions.e: Align Left lines the objects' left edges up along a common vertical line.

questions.q: How many total alignment options does PowerPoint offer (Left, Center, Right, Top, Middle, Bottom)?
questions.e: There are six alignment options in total.

questions.q: When 'Align to Slide' is active, alignment commands position objects relative to what?
o: The edges/center of the entire slide
Each other only, ignoring the slide
questions.e: Align to Slide uses the whole slide as the reference for positioning objects.

questions.q: When 'Align Selected Objects' is active, alignment commands position objects relative to what?
o: Each other, based on their own combined area
The printer margins on the page
The theme colors applied to it
questions.e: Align Selected Objects aligns objects only relative to one another, ignoring the slide as a whole.

questions.q: What do Distribute Horizontally and Distribute Vertically do?
o: Space three or more selected objects evenly across a dimension
questions.e: These commands evenly space multiple selected objects across the horizontal or vertical dimension.

questions.q: Which Ribbon tab contains the Group command?
questions.e: Group is located on the Format tab.

questions.q: What does the Group command do to multiple selected objects?
o: Combines them into a single unit that moves and resizes as one
Aligns them to the slide center
Converts them into a picture file
questions.e: Grouping merges selected objects into one combined, movable/resizable unit.

questions.q: How do you reverse a Group action?
o: Press the Delete key to remove the group entirely
Select the group, open the Group command menu, and choose Ungroup
Restart PowerPoint completely and reopen it
Use Undo only, since nothing else works
questions.e: Ungroup, found in the same Group menu, splits a grouped unit back into separate objects.

questions.q: If you drag any part of a grouped object, what happens?
o: The entire group moves together, keeping relative positions fixed
Nothing happens until you press Enter
questions.e: Once grouped, dragging any part moves every object in the group as a single unit.

questions.q: Which Ribbon tab contains the Rotate command?
questions.e: Rotate is on the Format tab, alongside Align and Group.

questions.q: What happens when you point to a rotation option in the Rotate menu before clicking it?
o: A live preview of the rotation shows on the slide
questions.e: Pointing to a rotation option shows a live preview before you commit by clicking.

questions.q: By default, how are overlapping objects on a slide layered?
o: Based on the order in which they were inserted, later objects on top
Randomly each time the slide is viewed
By file size, largest on top
questions.e: Objects layer according to insertion order — later-inserted objects sit above earlier ones.

questions.q: Which command moves a selected object all the way to the top of the stack?
questions.e: Bring to Front jumps the object above every other object in one step.

questions.q: Which command moves a selected object just one layer toward the front, past the next object only?
questions.e: Bring Forward moves the object one position forward, not all the way to the top.

questions.q: Which command moves a selected object all the way to the bottom of the stack?
questions.e: Send to Back places the object beneath every other object in one step.

questions.q: Which command moves a selected object just one layer toward the back, past the next object only?
questions.e: Send Backward moves the object one position backward, not all the way to the bottom.

questions.q: In a three-object stack diagram of Back → Middle → Front, which object was inserted first?
questions.e: The first-inserted object sits at the back of the default stacking order.

questions.q: Which pair of commands moves an object to the extreme top or bottom, versus one layer at a time?
o: Bring to Front/Send to Back vs Bring Forward/Send Backward
questions.e: Bring to Front and Send to Back are extreme moves; Bring Forward and Send Backward move one layer at a time.

questions.q: Which Ribbon tab and command let you insert a movie from a file?
o: Insert tab, Movie dropdown > Insert Movie from File
questions.e: Movies are inserted via Insert tab > Movie dropdown > Insert Movie from File.

questions.q: After selecting a movie file to insert, what choice must you make about playback?
o: Whether it plays Automatically or When Clicked
questions.e: PowerPoint asks whether the movie should play automatically or wait for a click.

questions.q: How is a movie object resized on the slide?
o: Only through a separate video-editing program
Using sizing handles, the same mechanics as resizing a picture
questions.e: Movies use the same corner/side sizing-handle mechanics as pictures.

questions.q: Which icon in a content placeholder lets you insert a movie without using the Insert tab?
questions.e: Content placeholders include an Insert Media Clip icon for inserting movies/media directly.

questions.q: How do you delete a movie or sound clip from a slide?
questions.e: Selecting the media clip and pressing Delete removes it from the slide.

questions.q: From which sources can sound be inserted into a PowerPoint slide?
o: Only from a file on the computer
From a file on the computer, from the clip organizer, or from audio CD tracks
Only from a live microphone recording
questions.e: PowerPoint supports inserting sound from a file, the clip organizer, or CD tracks.

questions.q: Like movies, sound clips can be set to play using which two trigger options?
questions.e: Sound clips share the same Automatically / When Clicked playback-trigger choice as movies.

questions.q: Which Audio Tools Options control lets you check a CD track's sound before the show runs?
questions.e: Preview plays the selected track so it can be checked in advance.

questions.q: Which Audio Tools Options setting offers Low, Medium, High or Mute?
questions.e: Volume controls the playback level with these four settings.

questions.q: Which Audio Tools Options fields are edited to set exactly which track and time point playback starts/stops at?
questions.e: The Track and Time fields let you specify exact CD track and time range for playback.

questions.q: Which Audio Tools Options command switches the playback trigger between Automatically and When Clicked?
questions.e: Change How to Play Track toggles between the two playback-trigger modes.

questions.q: Which Audio Tools Options setting hides the sound/CD icon so it does not appear during the slide show?
questions.e: Hide During Show keeps the audio icon invisible while presenting.

questions.q: Which slide view is the default view that opens when you start or open a presentation, letting you edit one slide at a time in the center pane?
questions.e: Normal View is PowerPoint's default view, showing the current slide in a center editing pane with a Slides tab down the left side.

questions.q: In Normal View, what is the narrow panel on the left side of the window, showing small thumbnails of every slide, called?
questions.e: The Slides tab lists thumbnails of all slides in order; clicking a thumbnail jumps to that slide, and dragging thumbnails reorders them.

questions.q: Which view displays miniature thumbnails of all the slides arranged in a grid, and is best for confirming the presentation is complete and correctly ordered?
questions.e: Slide Sorter View shows all slides as small thumbnails at once, making it easy to check completeness and drag-and-drop reorder them.

questions.q: How do you reorder slides while in Slide Sorter View?
o: Drag and drop a thumbnail to a new position
questions.e: Slide Sorter View supports reordering slides simply by dragging a thumbnail and dropping it in its new position.

questions.q: Which view shows the presentation full-screen, exactly as the audience will see it, with no editing menus visible?
questions.e: Slide Show View is used to rehearse or deliver a presentation full-screen, hiding all PowerPoint editing tools.

questions.q: In Slide Show View, which key or action moves to the NEXT slide?
questions.e: The Right Arrow key (along with Page Down, spacebar, or Enter) advances to the next slide or animation step during a slide show.

questions.q: In Slide Show View, which of these does NOT advance to the next slide?
questions.e: The Left Arrow key (and Page Up) moves to the PREVIOUS slide, not the next one.

questions.q: How do you end a slide show and return to the previous editing view?
questions.e: Pressing Esc during Slide Show View immediately ends the show and returns you to the view you were in before starting it.

questions.q: Which view mode would you use while actively writing and formatting the content of a single slide?
questions.e: Normal View is the working view for creating and editing slide content, one slide at a time in the main pane.

questions.q: A lecturer wants to quickly scan all 25 slides at once to make sure none are missing before class. Which view is best suited to this task?
questions.e: Slide Sorter View displays every slide as a thumbnail on one screen, making it ideal for confirming completeness and order.

questions.q: Which slide view would a presenter use to rehearse the timing and flow of a live delivery, exactly as an audience would experience it?
questions.e: Slide Show View presents the deck full-screen with no editing chrome, matching what the live audience will see.

questions.q: Which of the following is TRUE about the Slides tab in Normal View?
o: It replaces the need for Slide Show View
It only appears in Slide Sorter View
It can be used to reorder slides by dragging thumbnails
It shows speaker notes, not thumbnails
questions.e: The Slides tab in Normal View shows slide thumbnails and allows reordering by dragging them into a new position.

questions.q: Pressing Page Up during Slide Show View does what?
questions.e: Page Up (like the Left Arrow key) moves backward to the previous slide during a slide show.

questions.q: Where in PowerPoint do you go to preview and configure print settings for a presentation?
questions.e: Clicking the File tab opens Backstage view, and choosing Print there opens the Print Preview and Settings screen.

questions.q: On the Print Preview and Settings screen, which option lets you choose which physical printer the job is sent to?
questions.e: The Printer option lets you select which installed printer will receive the print job.

questions.q: Which print range option prints only the slide currently displayed?
questions.e: Print Current Slide restricts the print job to just the single slide that is currently open/displayed.

questions.q: Which print range option would you use to print only slides 4 through 9 of a 20-slide deck?
questions.e: A Custom Range lets you specify a particular slide range, such as 4-9, instead of printing the whole deck.

questions.q: What is the DEFAULT number of slides printed per page when using the Handouts layout?
questions.e: The Handouts layout defaults to 6 slide thumbnails per printed page, though this can be adjusted.

questions.q: Which Handouts option prints 3 slides per page WITH ruled lines beside each thumbnail for note-taking?
questions.e: The 3 Slides handout layout is specifically designed with space/lines next to each thumbnail so the audience can write notes.

questions.q: Which print layout shows ONE full slide per printed page, with no other slides or notes included?
questions.e: The Slides layout prints one full-size slide per page, making the slide itself the printed document.

questions.q: Which print layout prints a slide together with its speaker notes shown below it?
questions.e: Notes Pages prints one slide per page with the speaker notes for that slide printed underneath it.

questions.q: Notes Pages will only be useful for a presentation if which of these has already been done?
o: Adding speaker notes to the slides
questions.e: Notes Pages prints whatever speaker notes exist; if no notes were typed into the Notes pane, this layout has nothing extra to show.

questions.q: Which print layout prints the text content of all slides as a plain text outline, without pictures or slide graphics?
questions.e: The Outline layout prints only the text of the presentation in outline form, leaving out images and slide design.

questions.q: When printing Handouts, which of the following can be changed from the default arrangement?
o: The font used in Slide Show View
Slides-per-page count and horizontal vs. vertical layout
questions.e: Handout settings let you adjust how many slides appear per page and whether they are arranged horizontally or vertically.

questions.q: A student wants a cheap black-and-white paper copy of the whole deck to review before an exam, with room to write notes beside each slide. Which combination is most appropriate?
o: Notes Pages layout, color, Custom Range
3 Slides Handouts, grayscale, Print All Slides
Slides layout, color, Print Current Slide
questions.e: 3 Slides Handouts gives ruled note space beside each thumbnail, grayscale saves color ink, and Print All Slides covers the whole deck.

questions.q: On the Print Preview and Settings screen, which control changes whether the output is duplex (double-sided) instead of single-sided?
questions.e: Duplex/double-sided printing, along with paper size, is configured within the Print Settings options.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four standard print layout choices covered for PowerPoint?
questions.e: The standard print layouts are Slides, Handouts, Notes Pages, and Outline — Reading Layout is not one of them.

questions.q: What is animation, in the context of PowerPoint slides?
o: A way to rename a slide
Movement applied to text or an object within a single slide
questions.e: Animation refers to movement effects applied to text or objects inside one slide, such as text flying in or a shape spinning.

questions.q: Which of the following can animation effects be applied to?
o: Text, clip art, shapes, and pictures
questions.e: Animation can be applied broadly to text, clip art, shapes, and pictures on a slide.

questions.q: What are two key reasons for applying animation to text or objects?
o: To draw attention and improve readability
To increase file size and slow down the show
questions.e: Animation is used to draw the audience's attention to specific content and to improve readability by revealing information gradually.

questions.q: What is the first step in applying an animation effect to an object on a slide?
o: Select the object you want to animate
questions.e: Before an animation can be applied, the target text box, picture, shape, or clip art must first be selected on the slide.

questions.q: After selecting an object, which Ribbon tab do you use to apply an animation effect?
questions.e: Animation effects are chosen and applied from the gallery of effects on the Animations tab.

questions.q: When you apply an animation effect from the gallery, what happens automatically on the slide?
o: A live preview of the effect plays immediately
questions.e: PowerPoint plays a live preview of the chosen effect on the slide as soon as it is applied, so you can see it right away.

questions.q: To remove an animation effect from a selected object, what do you choose from the Animations tab's effect dropdown?
questions.e: Selecting None from the animation dropdown on the Animations tab removes the animation currently applied to that object.

questions.q: Which button do you use to choose an animation effect from a broader set of categories beyond the default gallery?
questions.e: The Add Animation button opens the full set of animation categories to choose from, beyond the quick gallery.

questions.q: Which animation category controls how an object FIRST appears on the slide?
questions.e: Entrance effects (such as Fade or Fly In) control how an object appears on the slide for the first time.

questions.q: Which animation category draws attention to an object that is already visible on the slide, without it entering or leaving?
questions.e: Emphasis effects (such as Pulse or Spin) highlight an object that is already on the slide, without it entering or exiting.

questions.q: Which animation category controls how an object LEAVES the slide?
questions.e: Exit effects (such as Fade Out or Fly Out) control how an object disappears from the slide.

questions.q: Which animation category makes an object travel along a defined line, curve, or custom-drawn route across the slide?
questions.e: Motion Path effects move an object along a specified path — straight, curved, or custom-drawn — across the slide.

questions.q: Which button lets you preview all of a slide's animations while staying in Normal View (not full-screen)?
questions.e: The Preview button on the Animations tab plays the slide's animations directly within Normal View.

questions.q: Which button previews a slide's animations exactly as the audience will see them, full-screen?
questions.e: Clicking Slide Show launches the full-screen view so animations can be checked exactly as the audience would experience them; press Esc to return.

questions.q: How do you return from a full-screen animation preview back to the editing view?
questions.e: Pressing Esc exits the full-screen Slide Show preview and returns you to the previous editing view.

questions.q: When a slide has several animated objects, where do you go to change the ORDER in which the effects play?
questions.e: The Custom Animation task pane lists all animations on the slide, with up/down arrows at the bottom to reorder them.

questions.q: In the Custom Animation task pane, how do you move a specific animation earlier or later in the play order?
o: Use the up/down arrows at the bottom of the pane
Rename the slide in the pane
Delete and retype the object's text
questions.e: The up and down arrows at the bottom of the Custom Animation task pane reorder the selected animation within the sequence.

questions.q: What is a transition, in PowerPoint terms?
o: Movement of text within a slide
Movement that happens between one slide and the next during Slide Show View
questions.e: A transition is the movement effect that occurs as the presentation moves from one slide to the next during a slide show.

questions.q: What is the key difference between an animation and a transition?
o: Transitions only work in Print Preview
Animation happens between slides; transition happens within a slide
There is no real difference, the terms are interchangeable
Animation is movement within a slide; transition is movement between slides
questions.e: Animation affects objects/text inside a single slide, while a transition affects the move from one slide to the next.

questions.q: Which Ribbon tab do you use to apply a transition to a slide?
questions.e: Slide transitions are applied and controlled from the Transitions tab.

questions.q: What is the DEFAULT setting shown in the Transition to This Slide group before any transition is chosen?
questions.e: Until a transition effect is chosen, the Transition to This Slide group shows No Transition as the default state.

questions.q: How do you open the full gallery of transition effects beyond the few shown by default?
questions.e: Clicking the More dropdown arrow in the Transitions group expands the complete gallery of available transition effects.

questions.q: What happens when you hover the mouse over a transition effect in the gallery, before clicking it?
o: A live preview of that transition plays on the slide
It automatically applies to all slides
questions.e: Hovering over a transition effect plays a live preview on the current slide so you can see it before committing to it.

questions.q: After choosing a transition effect for the current slide, which button applies that same transition to every slide in the presentation?
questions.e: The Apply To All button copies the currently selected slide's transition setting to every other slide in the deck.

questions.q: How do you remove a transition from just ONE slide?
o: Delete the slide and recreate it
Select None in the Transition to This Slide group
questions.e: Selecting None in the Transition to This Slide group removes the transition effect from that individual slide only.

questions.q: How do you remove transitions from EVERY slide in a presentation at once?
o: Select None, then click Apply To All
Select None on the first slide only
questions.e: Setting the transition to None and then clicking Apply To All clears the transition from every slide in the presentation.

questions.q: What does a small star icon beneath a slide thumbnail (in the Slides tab or Slide Sorter View) indicate?
o: The slide has a spelling error
The slide has a transition and/or animation applied
The slide is hidden from the show
questions.e: The star icon marks a slide that has a transition or animation applied, and clicking it plays a quick preview.

questions.q: Clicking the star icon beneath a slide thumbnail does what?
o: Opens Print Preview for that slide
Plays a preview of that slide's transition/animation
Marks the slide as the title slide
questions.e: Clicking the star icon previews the transition and/or animation effects on that slide without starting the full slide show.

questions.q: By default, how does a slide show advance to the next slide?
o: It cannot advance without editing the file
Only when the file is saved
questions.e: The default Advance Slide setting is On Mouse Click, meaning the presenter controls pacing manually (Enter also works).

questions.q: Which Transitions tab section lets you configure a slide to advance automatically after a set number of seconds?
questions.e: The Advance Slide section includes the Automatically After option for setting timed, hands-free advancement.

questions.q: Why would a presenter enable 'Automatically After' timed advancement instead of the default click-to-advance?
o: To make the file print faster
For unattended presentations, such as a looping trade-show or kiosk display
questions.e: Automatic timed advancement is especially useful when no presenter is available to click through slides, such as at a trade-show booth.

questions.q: Where can slide advance timing also be set and applied uniformly to every slide at once?
o: Slide Sorter View, using Apply to All
questions.e: Slide Sorter View lets you set a timing value and then use Apply to All so every slide advances after the same interval.

questions.q: A trainer is building a self-running kiosk demo with no one present to click through slides. What should they configure on the Transitions tab?
o: Automatically After timing in the Advance Slide section
questions.e: Setting Automatically After timing lets the presentation advance itself on a schedule, which is exactly what an unattended kiosk display needs.

questions.q: An Excel file that can contain one or more worksheets is called a:
questions.e: An Excel file is called a workbook, and it can contain multiple individual worksheets.

questions.q: Which bar displays the contents or formula of the currently active cell?
questions.e: The formula bar shows the raw content (value or formula) of whichever cell is currently selected.

questions.q: The small square at the bottom-right corner of a selected cell, used to copy data, is called the:
questions.e: Dragging the fill handle extends a series or copies a formula across adjacent cells.

questions.q: Which feature keeps specific rows or columns visible while scrolling through a large worksheet?
questions.e: Freeze Panes locks selected rows and/or columns in place so they remain visible during scrolling.

questions.q: The Quick Access Toolbar is used to:
o: Provide one-click access to frequently used commands
questions.e: It is a customizable toolbar that can hold shortcuts to commonly used commands, independent of the active ribbon tab.

questions.q: Which symbol locks a cell reference so it does not change when copied?
questions.e: The dollar sign fixes the row and/or column it precedes, creating an absolute or mixed reference.

questions.q: A reference that automatically adjusts when copied to a new cell is called a:
questions.e: Relative references shift based on their new position relative to the original formula cell.

questions.q: Which error appears when a formula attempts to divide a number by zero?
questions.e: #DIV/0! specifically indicates an attempted division by zero within a formula.

questions.q: The order in which Excel evaluates a formula's operations is known as:
questions.e: Excel follows standard mathematical precedence rules (parentheses, exponents, multiplication/division, then addition/subtraction).

questions.q: Which operator is used to join two text strings together in a formula?
questions.e: The ampersand (&) is the text concatenation operator in Excel formulas.

questions.q: Which function adds together all the numeric values in a specified range?
questions.e: SUM totals all numeric values within the given range of cells.

questions.q: Which function searches for a value in the first column of a range and returns a value from the same row?
questions.e: VLOOKUP performs a vertical lookup, searching down the first column of the specified table array.

questions.q: Which function returns TRUE only if every one of its supplied conditions is true?
questions.e: AND requires all listed conditions to be true simultaneously in order to return TRUE.

questions.q: Which function counts only the cells in a range that meet a specified condition?
questions.e: COUNTIF counts cells matching a single specified criterion within a range.

questions.q: Which function extracts a specified number of characters from the beginning of a text string?
questions.e: LEFT returns a set number of characters starting from the leftmost (first) character of the text.

questions.q: Which feature automatically formats cells that meet a specified rule, such as highlighting values above a threshold?
questions.e: Conditional formatting applies visual formatting automatically based on rules you define.

questions.q: Which tool copies formatting from one cell or range to another without copying its content?
questions.e: Format Painter copies only the formatting attributes, such as font and fill color, not the underlying data.

questions.q: Combining two or more selected cells into a single larger cell is called:
questions.e: Merge Cells joins the selected cells into one, typically centering the content across the merged area.

questions.q: Which formatting feature causes long text to display on multiple lines within a single cell?
questions.e: Wrap Text expands a cell's visible row height so overflowing text appears on additional lines instead of being cut off.

questions.q: Which setting determines whether a printed page is taller than wide, or wider than tall?
questions.e: Page orientation is set to either portrait (taller) or landscape (wider) in the Page Setup options.

questions.q: Which feature repeats specified rows or columns on every printed page of a large worksheet?
questions.e: Print Titles lets you designate header rows or columns that repeat automatically across all printed pages.

questions.q: The specific range of cells designated to actually be printed is called the:
questions.e: Only cells within the defined print area will appear in the printed output.

questions.q: Which view shows exactly how a worksheet will look when it is printed, before actually printing it?
questions.e: Print preview displays a simulated version of the final printed pages.

questions.q: Which file extension identifies a modern Excel workbook that can store macros?
questions.e: The .xlsm extension specifically denotes a macro-enabled Excel workbook.

questions.q: Which feature periodically saves a backup copy of a workbook in case of an unexpected crash?
questions.e: AutoRecover automatically creates recovery copies at set intervals to help prevent data loss.

questions.q: Which tool checks a workbook for hidden data or personal information before it is shared?
questions.e: Document Inspector scans for and helps remove metadata, comments, or hidden content before distribution.

questions.q: Which chart type is best suited for showing proportions of a whole, such as market share?
questions.e: Pie charts display data as proportional slices of a circle, ideal for part-to-whole comparisons.

questions.q: Sorting data from A to Z or smallest to largest is called:
questions.e: Ascending order arranges data from the lowest or earliest value to the highest or latest.

questions.q: Which feature displays only the rows meeting specified criteria while hiding the rest?
questions.e: Filtering temporarily hides rows that do not meet the chosen criteria, without deleting any data.

questions.q: Which chart type is best suited for showing a trend over time?
questions.e: Line charts connect data points with a continuous line, making trends over time easy to visualize.

questions.q: A predefined arrangement of placeholders on a slide is called a:
questions.e: Slide layouts define where placeholders like titles, text, and images appear on a given slide.

questions.q: Which view displays thumbnails of all slides for easy reordering?
questions.e: Slide Sorter view shows small previews of every slide, making it easy to rearrange their order.

questions.q: The master template that controls the overall design of all slides in a presentation is the:
questions.e: The Slide Master controls fonts, colors, and layouts inherited by every slide in the presentation.

questions.q: Which area below a slide is used to add speaker notes?
questions.e: The Notes pane provides space to write reminders or scripts that the presenter can reference.

questions.q: Which feature combines multiple selected shapes into a single manageable unit?
questions.e: Grouping objects lets you move, resize, or format several shapes together as one unit.

questions.q: Which tool automatically removes the background from an inserted picture?
questions.e: The Remove Background tool attempts to automatically detect and delete the background of an image.

questions.q: Which command moves a selected object above all others in the stacking order?
questions.e: Bring to Front places the selected object on top of any overlapping objects on the slide.

questions.q: SmartArt is primarily used to:
questions.e: SmartArt converts bulleted text into a variety of visual diagram layouts automatically.

questions.q: A visual effect that occurs when moving from one slide to the next is called a:
questions.e: Transitions apply to the change between two slides, while animations apply to individual objects within a slide.

questions.q: Which view allows a presenter to see their notes and upcoming slides while the audience only sees the current slide?
questions.e: Presenter view is designed to give the speaker helpful information not visible to the audience.

questions.q: Which type of animation controls how an object first appears on a slide?
questions.e: Entrance animations govern the way an object is introduced onto the slide.

questions.q: Which feature records how long each slide was displayed during a practice run-through?
questions.e: Rehearse Timings tracks the duration spent on each slide so it can later auto-advance during the actual show.

questions.q: When I formatted the cell containing the value 15389544, it changed to 1.54E+07. What formatting did I use?
questions.e: Scientific format displays large numbers in exponential notation, e.g. 1.54E+07.

questions.q: To copy formatting from a range of cells to more than one cell or range, first select the source range, then _____, and select the first and subsequent destination cells or ranges.
o: Click the format painter button on the Home tab.
Click the copy button on the Home tab
Double click the Copy button on the Home tab
Double click the format Painter button on the Home tab
Click the Paste button on the Home tab
questions.e: Double-clicking Format Painter keeps it active so it can be applied to several destinations in a row.

questions.q:
Which of these short-cut keys may be used to format text as italic?
I. Ctrl+3 II. Ctrl+4 III. Ctrl+5 IV. Ctrl+I
questions.e: Ctrl+3 and Ctrl+I both toggle italic formatting in Excel.

questions.q:
To center text across cells, one may use
I. Center Across Selection option in the Horizontal drop-down list of the Alignment tab of the Format Cells dialog box
II. The Merge and Center button from the alignment group under the Home tab
III. The Center button in the alignment group of the Home tab
questions.e: Center Across Selection and Merge & Center both center text over several cells; the plain Center button only centers within one cell.

questions.q: To make the cell height increase to contain multiple lines so that a lengthy text entry fits a cell, select the _____ check box on the alignment tab of the Format Cells dialog box.

The vertical drop-down list of the alignment option of the Format Cells dialog box has the following options:
I. General II. Left III. Bottom IV. Justify
questions.e: The vertical alignment list offers Top/Center/Bottom/Justify/Distributed — Bottom and Justify are valid, General and Left belong to the horizontal list.

questions.q: Under which tab of the Format Cells dialog box can you apply the Shrink To Fit option to a cell?
When the number 254500.5 is entered into a cell that is formatted as numeric with 2 d.p. and 1000 separator, what will be displayed in the cell when Enter is pressed?
Which of these is likely to be displayed in a cell that is formatted as GENERAL when the formula =NOW() is entered in the cell?
questions.e: The General format shows =NOW() as a readable date and time.

questions.q:
When you use the currency number format, you can specify _____.
I. the number of decimal places II. how you want to display negative numbers III. whether you want to use thousand separators IV. what currency symbol to use
questions.e: Currency formatting lets you set decimal places, negative-number display and the currency symbol; the thousands separator is fixed on for Currency.

questions.q: Which number format rounds numbers with decimals if the cell is not wide enough to show the entire number and also uses scientific notation for large numbers with at least 12 digits?
questions.e: General format automatically rounds/abbreviates or switches to scientific notation when a number doesn't fit the column width.
